scenarios.name: ADS_AccountLockout
scenarios.description: Use when a user or service account keeps getting locked out and you need to find which machine, process or failed logon sends the bad passwords; run it on a domain controller (only there are the KDC providers added) or on the suspected source machine. ETW traces (ADS_AccountLockout): Kerberos, NTLM and CredSSP, SSL/TLS (Schannel, NCrypt SSL and CAPI2) and LSA including the Netlogon provider; on a domain controller also the KDC. At start TSS sets the Security event log to 100 MB with overwrite (not restored at stop), enables success and failure auditing for 10 subcategories (Logon, Logoff, Account Lockout, Special Logon, Other Logon/Logoff Events, User Account Management, Kerberos Service Ticket Operations, Other Account Logon Events, Kerberos Authentication Service, Credential Validation) and turns on Netlogon debug logging (nltest /dbflag:0x2EBFFFFF). At stop it sets these audit subcategories to No Auditing (it does not restore the previous settings, so check auditpol /get /category:* afterwards) and turns Netlogon debug logging off (nltest /dbflag:0x0); it then exports the Security, System and Application event logs and copies the Netlogon logs (%windir%\debug\Netlogon.*), Lsass.log and the LSP logs (%windir%\debug\Lsp.*) if they exist, plus the environment variables and a process, service and file-version list. There is no network capture and no PSR; use ADS_AccountLockoutEx to add them.

scenarios.name: ADS_AccountLockoutEx
scenarios.description: Extended version of ADS_AccountLockout: use it when an account keeps getting locked out and, besides the authentication traces, you also need the network traffic of the failing logons or a record of the user's steps. It collects everything ADS_AccountLockout collects and adds a packet capture and PSR. ETW traces (ADS_AccountLockout): Kerberos, NTLM and CredSSP, SSL/TLS (Schannel, NCrypt SSL and CAPI2) and LSA including the Netlogon provider; on a domain controller also the KDC. At start TSS sets the Security event log to 100 MB with overwrite (not restored at stop), enables success and failure auditing for 10 logon, Kerberos, credential validation, account lockout and account management subcategories and turns on Netlogon debug logging (nltest /dbflag:0x2EBFFFFF). At stop it sets these subcategories to No Auditing (previous settings are not restored; check auditpol /get /category:*), turns Netlogon debug logging off (nltest /dbflag:0x0), exports the Security, System and Application event logs and copies the Netlogon logs (%windir%\debug\Netlogon.*), Lsass.log and the LSP logs if present, the environment variables and a process, service and file-version list. Tools (the difference from ADS_AccountLockout): a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus that scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions.

scenarios.name: ADS_ADLDS
scenarios.description: Use for AD LDS (Active Directory Lightweight Directory Services, formerly ADAM) problems on the AD LDS server, for example LDAP or LDAPS bind and authentication failures or certificate issues. ETW traces: AD LDS directory and LDAP server activity (ADS_ADLDS), Kerberos (ADS_Kerb), NTLM and CredSSP (ADS_NtLmCredSSP) and SSL/TLS with Schannel and CAPI2 (ADS_SSL). At start TSS enables and clears the CAPI2 and ESE Operational event logs (old content is saved to SavedEventLog) and turns on LSP debug logging (LspDbgInfoLevel and LspDbgTraceOptions under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa), which is not removed at stop. At stop, for each AD LDS instance (ADAM_* service) it collects the instance certificate store (certutil -verifystore -service), dcdiag /v /e and two ldifde exports (the msDS-Other-Settings object and the configuration partition) against the instance LDAP port, the ADAM_<instance> service registry key and the ADAM (<instance>) event log; it also collects the computer and user certificate stores, net accounts, Netsetup.log, adam*.log and Lsp.* from %windir%\debug, whoami /all, AuditPol, SecEdit and GPresult, and (from ADS_SSL) the CAPI2 log, Schannel events from the System log, the TLS, WinHTTP and .NET Framework registry settings, process lists at start and stop and a TLS test against www.ssllabs.com if the internet is reachable. Tools: a plain netsh packet capture (Netsh, no scenario providers), PerfMon DC counters (General, SMB, NET and Domain Controller counters such as NTDS and DirectoryServices) every 10 seconds and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog), so the full System, Application and Security event logs are not collected.

scenarios.name: ADS_Auth
scenarios.description: Use for sign-in and credential problems (Kerberos, NTLM, certificates, smart cards, Windows Hello for Business, Entra ID join or SSO) when the failing component is unknown; it uses the same code as the CSS auth scripts. ETW traces (ADS_Auth): Kerberos, NTLM and CredSSP, LSA with Netlogon, SAM, DPAPI and NCrypt, SSL/TLS, smart card, NGC (Windows Hello, TPM, device registration), biometrics, credential providers and web authentication (CloudAP, AAD, WAM, MSA, FIDO), plus GPSvc on build 22621 or later and the KDC on a domain controller. At start TSS enables about 25 authentication event logs (CAPI2 at 100 MB, Kerberos, KDC, AAD, Hello for Business, DPAPI and others; several are first saved to PreTraceLogs), enables debug logging (LSA to lsass.log, NegoExtender, PKU2U, LSP, Netlogon, GPSvc, certificate enrollment and NGC via certutil -setreg, Kerberos LogLevel on clients), saves dsregcmd, klist and netstat output and flushes the DNS cache. At stop it removes these debug settings and collects about 35 event logs (System, Application, NTLM, GroupPolicy and others, not Security), dsregcmd, klist, certificate store dumps (user, machine, NTAuth, root, CA), about 65 registry keys (Lsa, Kerberos, Schannel, Cryptography, Winlogon, Hello for Business), the Netlogon, lsass, LSP, gpsvc, Ngc and certificate enrollment logs, WAM token data, TPM logs, MDM diagnostics, SCCM logs, GPresult, hotfixes, whoami /all, nltest trusts, the secure channel on members, FSMO roles and the DC list on a DC and domain GPO attributes. Tools: a plain netsh packet capture (Netsh, no scenario providers); no PSR (use ADS_AuthEx). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). Options: -vAuth adds client NGC and WebAuth providers, -slowlogon adds a WPR slow logon trace, -whfb adds Hello for Business data (on a DC it prompts for a user name).

scenarios.name: ADS_AuthEx
scenarios.description: Extended version of ADS_Auth for sign-in and credential problems (Kerberos, NTLM, certificates, smart cards, Windows Hello for Business, Entra ID join or SSO) where you also want to see what the user does: it collects exactly what ADS_Auth collects and adds Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions; that is the only difference. ETW traces (ADS_Auth): Kerberos, NTLM and CredSSP, LSA with Netlogon, SAM, DPAPI and NCrypt, SSL/TLS, smart card, NGC (Windows Hello, TPM, device registration), biometrics, credential providers and web authentication (CloudAP, AAD, WAM, MSA, FIDO), plus GPSvc on build 22621 or later and the KDC on a domain controller. At start TSS enables about 25 authentication event logs, enables debug logging (LSA to lsass.log, NegoExtender, PKU2U, LSP, Netlogon, GPSvc, certificate enrollment and NGC, Kerberos LogLevel on clients), saves dsregcmd, klist and netstat output and flushes the DNS cache. At stop it removes these debug settings and collects about 35 event logs (not Security), dsregcmd, klist, certificate store dumps, about 65 registry keys, the Netlogon, lsass, LSP, gpsvc, Ngc and certificate enrollment logs, WAM, TPM, MDM and SCCM data, GPresult, hotfixes, whoami /all, nltest trusts, the secure channel on members, FSMO roles and the DC list on a DC and domain GPO attributes. Tools: a plain netsh packet capture (Netsh, no scenario providers) and PSR. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). Options: -vAuth, -slowlogon (WPR slow logon trace) and -whfb (on a DC it prompts for a user name) work as in ADS_Auth.

scenarios.name: ADS_Basic
scenarios.description: Use for authentication problems (Kerberos, NTLM, certificates and smart cards, Windows Hello for Business, cloud sign-in, EFS or DPAPI) when you want the authentication traces and logs without a network capture. ETW traces (ADS_Basic): Kerberos, NTLM and CredSSP, LSA with Netlogon, DPAPI and NCrypt, crypto primitives (BCrypt, CNG, CAPI), EFS, SSL/TLS, smart card, NGC (Windows Hello, TPM, device registration), biometrics, credential providers and web authentication (CloudAP, AAD, WAM, MSA, FIDO); on a domain controller also the KDC. At start TSS saves and then enables 9 event logs (CAPI2 at 100 MB, Kerberos, KDC, KdcProxy, WebAuth, WebAuthN, Biometrics, HelloForBusiness, CertPoleEng), enables debug logging (LSA to lsass.log, NegoExtender, PKU2U, LSP, Kerberos LogLevel, Schannel EventLogging, Netlogon, GPSvc, Folder Redirection, Security CSE winlogon.log, certificate enrollment and NGC via certutil -setreg) and saves dsregcmd, tasklist, services, klist, ipconfig and netstat output. At stop it removes these settings again (Schannel EventLogging is set to 1), exports those event logs plus System, Application and GroupPolicy, and collects klist, ipconfig, netstat, the Ngc, Netlogon, lsass, LSP, Netsetup, gpsvc, CertEnroll and winlogon logs, cmdkey /list, about 40 registry keys (Lsa, Schannel, Cryptography, Winlogon, KDC, Winbio, PassportForWork, FIDO, DeviceGuard), netsh http sslcert and urlacl, nltest trusts and (not on a DC) the secure channel, certutil dumps of the user, machine, smart card, NTAuth, root and CA stores, scheduled tasks, services, fltmc, GPresult, versions of 16 security DLLs and hotfixes. There is no network capture and no PSR; use ADS_BasicEx to add them.

scenarios.name: ADS_BasicEx
scenarios.description: Extended version of ADS_Basic: use it for authentication problems (Kerberos, NTLM, certificates and smart cards, Windows Hello for Business, cloud sign-in, EFS or DPAPI) when you also need the network traffic and a record of the user's steps. It collects everything ADS_Basic collects and adds a packet capture and PSR. ETW traces (ADS_Basic): Kerberos, NTLM and CredSSP, LSA with Netlogon, DPAPI and NCrypt, crypto primitives, EFS, SSL/TLS, smart card, NGC (Windows Hello, TPM, device registration), biometrics, credential providers and web authentication (CloudAP, AAD, WAM, MSA, FIDO); on a domain controller also the KDC. At start TSS saves and enables 9 authentication event logs (CAPI2 at 100 MB, Kerberos, KDC, WebAuthN, Biometrics, HelloForBusiness and others), enables debug logging (LSA to lsass.log, NegoExtender, PKU2U, LSP, Kerberos LogLevel, Schannel EventLogging, Netlogon, GPSvc, Folder Redirection, Security CSE, certificate enrollment and NGC) and saves dsregcmd, tasklist, services, klist, ipconfig and netstat output. At stop it removes these settings again (Schannel EventLogging is set to 1), exports those event logs plus System, Application and GroupPolicy, and collects the Ngc, Netlogon, lsass, LSP, Netsetup, gpsvc, CertEnroll and winlogon logs, cmdkey /list, about 40 registry keys, netsh http sslcert and urlacl, nltest trusts and (not on a DC) the secure channel, certutil dumps of the certificate stores, scheduled tasks, services, fltmc, GPresult, security DLL versions and hotfixes. Tools (the difference from ADS_Basic): a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus that scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions.

scenarios.name: ADS_DFSR
scenarios.description: Use for DFS Replication problems (SYSVOL or replicated folders not replicating, backlogs, conflicts, database or staging issues) on a domain controller or DFSR member server when you need a DFSR configuration and health snapshot. The DFS Replication component (ADS_DFSR) has no active ETW providers (they are commented out), so no DFSR trace is recorded and nothing is captured while TSS waits at the repro prompt; all data comes from scripts\DfsrInfo.ps1, which TSS runs at stop into the DfsrInfo folder and stops after 600 seconds (change with -DFSRTimeout). DfsrInfo.ps1 collects OS, hotfix, volume, DFSR database and network information, the replication groups, folders, members, connections and version vectors, conflict and deleted items, local sync and SYSVOL state, the DFSR Active Directory configuration, FSRM screens and quotas, DFSR performance data, DfsrMachineConfig.xml and the System Volume Information\DFSR\Config files, the DFSR, TCP/IP and RPC registry keys, the zipped DFSR debug logs (%windir%\debug\Dfsr*), the DFS Replication, System and Application event logs (plus Directory Service on a DC) as EVTX and CSV, DfsrAdmin health reports when DfsrAdmin.exe exists, and on a DC dcdiag /v and repadmin /showrepl and /replsum; it also writes a dfsrs.exe dump if DFSR events 1315 or 1316 occurred since boot. Use -DFSRParams to pass DfsrInfo options such as -ForceDump (always dump dfsrs.exe) or -Backlog All, Incoming or Outgoing (backlog report). DfsrInfo.ps1 exits without data if the WinRM or DFS Replication service is not running. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). There is no network capture, PerfMon, Procmon or WPR; use ADS_DFSREx for those.

scenarios.name: ADS_DFSREx
scenarios.description: Extended version of ADS_DFSR: use it for DFS Replication performance problems (slow replication, growing backlog, high CPU, disk or network use by DFSR) when you need activity recorded during the repro in addition to the DFSR snapshot. It collects everything ADS_DFSR collects: the DFS Replication component (ADS_DFSR) has no active ETW providers, and at stop TSS runs scripts\DfsrInfo.ps1 into the DfsrInfo folder (DFSR configuration, replication groups, connections, version vectors, conflicts, SYSVOL state, DFSR debug and event logs, DFSR registry, DfsrAdmin health reports, on a DC dcdiag and repadmin, and a dfsrs.exe dump if DFSR events 1315 or 1316 occurred since boot), stopped after 600 seconds unless -DFSRTimeout is used; -DFSRParams passes options such as -ForceDump or -Backlog All. DfsrInfo.ps1 needs the WinRM and DFS Replication services running. Tools (the difference from ADS_DFSR): a Performance Monitor counter log with the DFSR set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB server and client, network adapter, and DFS Replicated Folders, Connections and Service Volumes counters) every 15 seconds, plus a long-term counter log with the same set every 5 minutes; a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilter, network and registry); Process Monitor (file, registry and process activity in a ring buffer, 3096 MB by default); and a plain netsh packet capture (Netsh, no scenario providers). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: ADS_ESR
scenarios.description: Use when Enterprise State Roaming (ESR), the cloud sync of Windows settings on Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) joined devices, fails or does not sync. ETW traces: Enterprise State Roaming (ADS_ESR), one component that combines the Connected Devices Platform (CDP), CloudStore, ShellRoaming/SettingSync-Azure, web authentication (CloudAP, AAD, TokenBroker/WAM, Microsoft account), SSL/Schannel and WinHTTP providers; the ETL is circular with a 4096 MB limit (EtlOptions circular:4096), so TSS can run for a long time until the issue occurs. At start TSS saves the build info, ipconfig /all and the task list, flushes the DNS cache and enables the CAPI2/Operational, CloudStore/Debug, AAD Analytic and Operational, User Device Registration Debug and Admin and PushNotification-Platform Debug and Admin event logs. At stop it runs dsregcmd /status (also /debug /all), disables those event logs and exports them plus CloudStore/Operational, and saves the task list, the DNS cache (ipconfig /displaydns), the environment variables and the HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System registry keys (CDPlogs folder); with -CustomParams <user name> it also copies that user's AppData\Local\ConnectedDevicesPlatform folder. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Process Monitor (Procmon) with a 1000 MB ring buffer (ProcMonRingBufferSize 1000). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). Side effect: the event logs are not restored to their previous state, so AAD/Operational and User Device Registration/Admin, which Windows enables by default, stay disabled after TSS stops.

scenarios.name: ADS_GPOEx
scenarios.description: Use for in-depth Group Policy problems: policies or Group Policy Preferences (GPP) not applying, slow or failing policy processing, or errors when editing GPOs (Group Policy editor, GPMC). ETW traces: Group Policy processing, the client-side extensions and the Security Configuration Engine (ADS_GPO); ADS_GPsvc, ADS_GPedit and ADS_GPmgmt have no ETW providers and switch on debug logs instead. At start TSS enables GPP logging and tracing for all preference extensions (User.log, Computer.log and Planning.log in the system drive root), security extension debug logging (winlogon.log), Group Policy service debug logging (gpsvc.log), Netlogon debug logging (nltest /dbflag:0x2EBFFFFF), Group Policy editor, GPText, Administrative Templates and GPMC debug logging, and exports HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft. At stop it collects these logs (debug\usermode with gpsvc.log, netlogon.log, GPP logs, winlogon.log, AdmTmpl.log, GPMgmt logs), Audit.csv, the security templates\policies folder, the Group Policy Operational, Application and System event logs, GPresult (/h, /v, /r), AuditPol and SecEdit exports, the AD attributes of all domain GPOs and the GPExtensions, Policies and printer registry keys. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) with a 1000 MB ring buffer (ProcMonRingBufferSize 1000) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). Run gpupdate during the repro so the GPP logs are written. At stop the debug settings are removed again, but the Netlogon debug flag is set to 0 (not restored) and the whole HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Group Policy key is deleted, including values set by real policies, until the next Group Policy refresh.

scenarios.name: ADS_OCSP
scenarios.description: Use on an Online Responder (OCSP) server when certificate revocation requests to it fail, are slow or return an unexpected status. ETW traces: the Online Responder service, web proxy and revocation provider (ADS_OCSP), HTTP.sys, WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_HttpSys), SSL/TLS with Schannel and NcryptSslp (ADS_SSL) and IIS, ASP.NET and WAS (NET_IIS). At start TSS enables OCSP debug logging (certutil -setreg -f Debug 0xffffffe3), runs IISreset, restarts the OCSPsvc service, saves and clears the CAPI2/Operational event log and enables it, and lists processes and services. At stop it sets the debug flag back to 0, runs IISreset and restarts OCSPsvc again, then collects OCSPsvc.log (ServiceProfiles\NetworkService), a text conversion of the OCSP ETL (netsh trace convert), the CAPI2/Operational log, the Schannel events of the System log, the HTTPERR and inetpub IIS logs, netsh http show servicestate, sslcert and urlacl, appcmd lists of the IIS configuration, sites, application pools and applications, the OcspSvc, HTTP.sys service, Schannel/TLS, WinHTTP auto-proxy service and .NET Framework registry keys, the process list and, if www.ssllabs.com is reachable, a TLS client test page. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR). Side effects: IIS and the OCSP service restart at start and at stop, which briefly interrupts revocation responses, and CAPI2/Operational stays enabled after TSS.

scenarios.name: ADS_Profile
scenarios.description: Use for user profile problems: slow logon or logoff, temporary or corrupt profiles, roaming profile or folder redirection failures, profile cleanup, or FSLogix profile containers. ETW traces: the User Profile Service and user manager (ADS_Profile), Folder Redirection (ADS_FolderRedirection), Group Policy processing and client-side extensions (ADS_GPO) and the FSLogix services and drivers (UEX_FSLogix); ADS_GPsvc has no ETW providers and only switches on debug logging. At start TSS enables the User Profile Service/Diagnostic event log, Group Policy Preferences tracing (User.log, Computer.log, Planning.log), security extension (winlogon.log), Administrative Templates, Group Policy service (gpsvc.log) and Netlogon (nltest /dbflag:0x2EBFFFFF) debug logging. At stop it collects the Group Policy, User Profile Service (Operational, Diagnostic), Folder Redirection, Application and System event logs, GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit, a profile age report (ADS_ProfileAge.log with the load, unload and cleanup dates of every profile), gpsvc.log, netlogon.log, the GPP and winlogon logs, the AD attributes of domain GPOs, the GPExtensions, Policies and printer registry keys, and FSLogix data (logs, event logs, frx list-redirects and list-rules, FSLogix, Office, OneDrive, Windows Search and ProfileList registry, whoami /all, FSLogix group memberships). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). At stop the debug settings are removed again, but the Netlogon debug flag is set to 0 and the whole HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Group Policy key is deleted until the next Group Policy refresh.

scenarios.name: ADS_Replication
scenarios.description: Use on domain controllers when Active Directory replication fails or is slow, objects or schema changes do not replicate, or replication shows Kerberos errors. ETW traces: the Active Directory Domain Services core (ADS_ADDS), ADSI (ADS_Schema), the Kerberos client (ADS_Kerb) and the Kerberos KDC (ADS_KDC, only active on a DC). On a DC, TSS raises the NTDS diagnostic logging levels 5 Replication Events, 9 Internal Processing and 24 DS Schema to 5 at start and sets them to 0 at stop. At stop it collects klist tickets (user, SYSTEM, NetworkService), cmdkey /list, tasklist, the Lsa, Netlogon, SecurityProviders, Winlogon, profile and Policies registry keys, the PolicyDefinitions and adprep folders, the dcpromo, netlogon, netsetup and winlogon logs, audit.csv and netlogon.dns; on domain members and DCs also nltest secure channel, DC list, site and trust queries, netdom query fsmo, setspn duplicate SPN checks and a SYSVOL listing with ACLs. On a DC it adds dcdiag /v, repadmin (showrepl, queue, failcache, showconn, showvector, showobjmeta and more), ntfrsutl, dsacls of each partition, ldifde exports of the configuration, System and Domain Controllers containers and of the schema (Schema.ldf), the partial attribute set, AD PowerShell exports (forest, domain, DCs, sites, subnets, site links, trusts, password policies, replication failures and queue, GPOs), the NTDS registry key and the Directory Service event log. It also saves dsregcmd /status, GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit. Tools: a netsh packet capture (Netsh). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: ADS_SBSL
scenarios.description: Use for slow boot or slow logon (SBSL) caused by Group Policy, profiles, authentication or DC discovery. ETW traces: DC discovery (NET_DCLocator), the authentication stack with Kerberos, NTLM, LSA, Schannel, web authentication, NGC, smart card and DPAPI (ADS_Auth), the User Profile Service (ADS_Profile), Group Policy processing (ADS_GPO) and Netlogon (NET_Netlogon); ADS_GPsvc has no ETW providers and only enables debug logging. At start TSS enables about 25 authentication-related event logs (CAPI2 and Kerberos are cleared first) and the User Profile Service/Diagnostic log; turns on LSA, LSP, Kerberos, Netlogon, Group Policy service (gpsvc.log), Group Policy Preferences, security extension, Administrative Templates, certificate enrollment and NGC debug logging; saves pre-trace dsregcmd and klist output; and flushes the DNS cache. At stop it exports the event logs and collects lsass.log, the Windows\debug folder (netlogon.log, gpsvc.log, lsp.log), the GPP and winlogon logs, GPresult, AuditPol, SecEdit, a profile age report, domain GPO attributes, dsregcmd, klist, certificate stores, TPM and MDM data, about 60 authentication registry keys, the Offline Files (CSC), TCP/IP, Schannel/TLS and WinHTTP auto-proxy keys and a few Netlogon, TCP/IP, MUP, Winlogon and LSA values (Reg_UNChard1.txt). Tools: WPR with the SBSL profile (config\sbsl.wprp: CPU, disk, memory and handle activity plus Winlogon, Group Policy, profile and Shell-Core events) and a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers). The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). The debug settings are removed at stop, but the Netlogon debug flag is set to 0 and the HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Group Policy key is deleted until the next Group Policy refresh.

scenarios.name: ADS_SSL
scenarios.description: Use when TLS/SSL connections fail or behave unexpectedly on this machine, for example HTTPS, LDAPS or RDP handshake failures, protocol or cipher suite mismatches, or certificate trust errors. ETW traces: SSL/TLS (ADS_SSL) with the Schannel, Schannel events, NcryptSslp and SSL providers. At start TSS saves and clears the CAPI2/Operational event log and enables it, and lists the running processes and services. At stop it restores the previous CAPI2/Operational settings and exports the log, exports the Schannel events of the System log (evt_schannel.evtx), lists processes and services again, and exports the Schannel/TLS registry keys (SecurityProviders\Schannel, SSL cipher suite configuration, FipsAlgorithmPolicy), the WinHTTP auto-proxy service key and the .NET Framework v2/v4 keys (non-recursive). If www.ssllabs.com is reachable and the machine is not an NPS (IAS) server, it also downloads the SSL Labs client test page (TestConn_TLS.html), which shows the TLS versions and cipher suites offered by the .NET client. Tools: a netsh packet capture (Netsh), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: ADS_WinLAPS
scenarios.description: Use for Windows LAPS problems: the local administrator password is not rotated, not backed up to Active Directory or Microsoft Entra ID, cannot be retrieved or decrypted, or the LAPS policy does not apply. ETW traces: Windows LAPS (ADS_WinLAPS) and the authentication stack with Kerberos, NTLM, LSA, Schannel, web authentication, NGC, smart card and DPAPI providers (ADS_Auth). At start TSS enables about 25 authentication-related event logs (CAPI2 and Kerberos are cleared first), turns on LSA, LSP, Kerberos, Netlogon, Group Policy service, certificate enrollment and NGC debug logging, saves pre-trace dsregcmd and klist output and flushes the DNS cache. At stop it removes these debug settings again (the Netlogon debug flag is set to 0) and collects the LAPS/Operational event log, the LAPS registry keys (LAPS policies, Config and State, legacy AdmPwd policy, LAPS client-side extension), copies of the LAPS DLLs and Samsrv.dll, GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit, plus the authentication data: the exported authentication event logs, lsass.log, netlogon.log, lsp.log, gpsvc.log, dsregcmd, klist, certificate stores, TPM and MDM data, about 60 authentication registry keys, domain GPO attributes, hotfixes and whoami /all. Tools: a netsh packet capture (Netsh) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR).

scenarios.name: CRM_General
scenarios.description: Use for Microsoft Dynamics CRM problems when the failing area is not yet known, for example errors, slowness or hangs of the CRM web application. The scenario has no ETW components and does not enable CRM platform tracing (use CRM_Platform for that); it gathers generic data with tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's internet client ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, a Windows Performance Recorder trace with the General profile (WPR General: CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilters, network and registry), Performance Monitor counters of the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. At the end TSS builds an SDP CRMBase report. Note: CRMBase is a deprecated SDP type without own collectors; in a normal interactive run TSS silently uses the NET SDP collectors instead, but when the trace is stopped by a separate .\TSS.ps1 -Stop run, TSS prints 'SDP CRMBase is deprecated: Please no longer use this SDP report.' and exits at the SDP step without an SDP report and without zipping the results (add -noSDP to the -Stop command to avoid this).

scenarios.name: CRM_IISdump
scenarios.description: Intended for crashes or hangs of the Dynamics CRM web front end (its IIS application pool), but the dump collection is not implemented yet: the CRM_IISdump component (CRM_IISdump) has no ETW providers and its start and collect functions only print '...Not implemented - Coming soon', so no memory dump and no CRM or IIS data are collected. In practice the scenario only records Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions and a screen video while you reproduce the issue. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). To get a dump of the CRM application pool, use the TSS -ProcDump option with the PID of its w3wp.exe worker process instead.

scenarios.name: CRM_Platform
scenarios.description: Use for Microsoft Dynamics CRM platform errors or slow operations (server-side business logic, or the CRM client) when you need the CRM platform trace files. The CRM_Platform component (CRM_Platform) has no ETW providers; it switches on the built-in CRM file tracing instead: at start it sets verbose tracing in the registry (TraceEnabled=1, TraceCategories=*:Verbose, TraceCallStack=1, TraceFileSizeLimit=100 and an incremented TraceRefresh) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\MSCRMClient on a CRM client (HKCU of the account running TSS) and under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\MSCRM on a CRM server. At stop it sets TraceEnabled=0 and TraceRefresh back and, on a server, re-saves CRMWeb\web.config in the CRM install folder so that CRM picks up the change (ASP.NET restarts the CRM web application). It then tries to copy the *.log trace files written in the last 24 hours from %USERPROFILE%\Local Settings\Application Data\Microsoft\MSCRM\Traces (client) and %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Dynamics CRM\Trace (server); because of a code defect this copy fails on Windows PowerShell 5.1, so check the output and copy the recent trace files manually if they are missing. Tools: Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). Run it on the CRM server or client where the problem occurs.

scenarios.name: DEV_EESummitDemo
scenarios.description: EE Summit 2023 demo scenario, kept for demonstrating and testing the TSS framework; do not use it for customer data collection (use ADS_Auth or other ADS scenarios for real Kerberos or Netlogon problems). ETW traces: Netlogon (NETLOGON/NETLIB and Microsoft-Windows-Security-Netlogon) and W32Time providers (DEV_EESummitDemo) and the Kerberos client (ADS_Kerb). At start it enables the Netlogon debug log (Netlogon\Parameters DbFlag = _NetLogonFlag from tss_config.cfg, 0x2FFFFFFF by default) and sets DbFlag back to 0 at stop. At stop, on a domain member or DC that can reach a DC, it runs nltest /dclist, /dsgetsite, /domain_trusts and /trusted_domains and w32tm /query status, configuration and peers; it also collects AuditPol, SecEdit and GPresult output, the dcpromo, dcpromoui, netlogon and netsetup logs from %SystemRoot%\debug, the W32Time, Netlogon\Parameters and LAPS GP extension registry keys and the Application, System and Directory Service event logs (this collection runs twice, as component log and as scenario log). Tools: a plain netsh packet capture (Netsh) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: DEV_General
scenarios.description: Internal developer scenario for testing the TSS framework (a general-purpose template with the NET common tasks); not for customer data collection, use the POD-specific scenarios instead. It has no ETW components; it runs only generic tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, Performance Monitor counters of the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: DEV_Scn1
scenarios.description: Internal developer test scenario 1 for the TSS framework, not for customer data collection: it checks that TSS starts and stops a simple single-ETL component and calls every scenario and component hook. ETW traces: the LSA and Kerberos providers in one ETL file (DEV_TEST1). All six scenario hooks (DEV_Scn1ScenarioPreStart, PostStart, PreStop, PostStop, CollectDEV_Scn1ScenarioLog and RunDEV_Scn1ScenarioDiag) and the DEV_TEST1 start and stop hooks only write an 'is called' line to the TSS log; the component log and diag functions do not run because the scenario has no CollectComponentLog. TSS collects its default basic log at stop. The scenario definition also holds a commented-out catalog of almost every TSS switch, which developers enable when testing.

scenarios.name: DEV_Scn2
scenarios.description: Internal developer test scenario 2 for the TSS framework, not for customer data collection: it tests a scenario definition that depends on the product type and components that write one or several ETL files. ETW traces on a client (product type WinNT): LSA and Kerberos providers in one ETL (DEV_TEST1), certificate client, certification authority and LSA providers split into CertCli, CertificationAuthority and lsa ETL files with per-provider flags and levels (DEV_TEST2), two LSA providers with different flags in one ETL (DEV_TEST3) and LSA plus certification authority providers in two ETLs (DEV_TEST4); DEV_TEST5 is disabled and the UEX_Task key is ignored. On servers and domain controllers it traces only DEV_TEST1 and DEV_TEST2. The scenario and component hooks only write 'is called' lines to the TSS log, except that on a client the DEV_TEST3 stop hook tries to copy test files from hard-coded developer paths under C:\Subst_E (normally missing, so only warnings are logged). No component logs are collected (no CollectComponentLog); TSS collects its default basic log at stop.

scenarios.name: DEV_Scn3
scenarios.description: Internal developer test scenario 3 for the TSS framework, not for customer data collection: it tests a single component that writes several ETL files, using the GUID!file!flags!level provider syntax. ETW traces: certificate client, certification authority and LSA providers split into CertCli, CertificationAuthority and lsa ETL files with per-provider flags and levels (DEV_TEST2). The DEV_TEST2 start and stop hooks only write 'is called' lines to the TSS log, the scenario has no scenario hooks, and no component log is collected (no CollectComponentLog). TSS collects its default basic log at stop.

scenarios.name: DND_Power
scenarios.description: Use for power problems: battery drain, sleep, hibernate or resume failures, unexpected wakes, Modern Standby or power plan issues. ETW traces: 29 power providers (DND_Power): power policy and power requests, processor power profiles, battery, sleep study and screen-on study, selective suspend, energy estimation, the power control panel and powercfg, the user-mode power service and the Power Dependency Coordinator. Tools: a Windows Performance Recorder trace with the built-in Power profile (WPR Power). At stop it runs the full DND Setup Report into the Setup_Report folder (about 26 default phases such as Windows Update, CBS and PnP servicing, setup and upgrade logs, activation, BitLocker, Defender, Device Guard, AppLocker, MDM, Delivery Optimization, storage, process, basic network, permissions and policies, event logs, minidumps, reliability summary and performance data), including the power configuration (powercfg /L, /aliases, /a, /qh and the Control\Power, Session Manager\Power, Shell\USB and USB AutomaticSurpriseRemoval registry keys). The detailed power reports this scenario is meant to add (powercfg /batteryreport, /energy, /sleepstudy on Modern Standby devices, /srumutil, /systempowerreport, /requests, /waketimers, /lastwake, wake-armed devices and abnormal sleep study ETLs) are only produced when the Setup Report runs its phases sequentially (_DND_SETUPReport_UseRunspaces=0 in tss_config.cfg); in the default parallel (runspace) mode they are skipped. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: DND_Servicing
scenarios.description: Use for Windows servicing problems: cumulative or standalone updates, servicing stack updates, features on demand, language packs or driver packages that fail to install, uninstall or hang (CBS, DISM or Windows Update errors). ETW traces: 25 providers for Component Based Servicing (CBS), Plug and Play and driver installation (PnP manager, SetupAPI, DriverStore) and Windows Update (DND_Servicing). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode to record file and registry activity during the servicing operation. At stop it collects into the Servicing folder: msinfo32 (.nfo) and systeminfo; a copy of the COMPONENTS hive; the CBS and DISM logs, setupapi logs (inf\*.log), poqexec.log (also with converted timestamps), pending.xml, the servicing session XML files, UpdateAgent.log, lpksetup.log and iemain.log; directory listings of WinSxS, WinSxS\temp, servicing and dism; DISM output (packages with per-package details, features, capabilities, editions, international settings, drivers and /CheckHealth), Get-WindowsDriver and Win32_PnPEntity lists and a list of update packages in a broken CBS state; on Windows 10 and later pnputil /export-pnpstate, driverquery /si and the ComputerIds (CHID) registry key; the SideBySide and Component Based Servicing registry hives (reg save, can take several minutes), the TrustedInstaller service settings, a check for drivers missing from the DriverStore and a summary of problematic sessions in sessions.xml. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: INT_General
scenarios.description: Use for BizTalk Server and other integration problems when the failing area is not yet known, for example errors, slowness or hangs of an integration application. The scenario has no ETW components and no product-specific log collection; it gathers generic data with tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's internet client ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, a Windows Performance Recorder trace with the General profile (WPR General: CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilters, network and registry), Performance Monitor counters of the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. For Message Queuing problems use INT_MSMQ instead.

scenarios.name: INT_MSMQ
scenarios.description: Use for Microsoft Message Queuing (MSMQ) problems, for example messages that are not sent, routed, delivered or received, transactional queue issues or MSMQ service errors (also when MSMQ is used by BizTalk). ETW traces: 17 MSMQ providers (INT_MSMQ): the MSMQ and MSMQ Triggers event providers plus the internal MSMQ trace areas (general, AC driver, networking, SRMP, RPC, directory service, security, routing, transactions, logging, profiling and error logging). At stop it collects the HKLM\Software\Microsoft\MSMQ registry key and an MSMQInfo file with the installed MSMQ features, the system locale and user languages, the mqqm.dll and mqac.sys versions and the permissions of the MSMQ registry key and the C:\Windows\System32\MSMQ folder; on a server with the RSAT-AD-PowerShell feature it also exports the Active Directory properties of the computer object and its MSMQ configuration object (CN=msmq). The TMQ.exe queue state, site and store output that should follow is currently skipped because of a code defect. Tools: Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the INT common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: NET_802Dot1x
scenarios.description: Use when a wired LAN client fails IEEE 802.1X (dot3) authentication, for example EAP or certificate errors on a switch port (for WiFi use NET_WLAN). ETW traces: Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, with a TCP rundown at start and stop and a port exhaustion check at stop), NDIS (NET_NDIS), Radio Manager (NET_RadioManager), Windows Connection Manager (NET_WCM), the network connect UI (NET_NetworkUX) and Schannel TLS (ADS_SSL, which enables and clears the CAPI2 log at start). At start and stop TSS saves netsh wlan show outputs and exports the LAN profiles. At stop it adds the dot3svc, WlanSvc, EapHost, Rasman and wired/wireless policy, Schannel/TLS, WinHTTP auto-proxy and .NET registry keys; dot3svc policy files, wlansvc profiles and connection phonebooks; the Wired-AutoConfig, Wcmsvc, NetworkProfile, GroupPolicy, CAPI2 and Security event logs plus Schannel System events; certificate stores and the cmdkey list; Credential Guard state; driverquery; a TLS test to www.ssllabs.com; on build 16299+ the WLAN report HTML. Tools: netsh trace with the dot3_wpp and wireless_dbg scenarios at full level plus CAPI2, EapHost and two more providers by GUID (packet capture plus ETW), RAS diagnostic tracing (RASdiag), Process Monitor, PSR and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. With a Surface Marvell WiFi adapter (mrvlpcie8897) TSS sets driver debug registry values at start (a reboot is needed the first time) and removes them at stop.

scenarios.name: NET_BITS
scenarios.description: Use when Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) jobs fail, stall or transfer slowly, for example Windows Update, Configuration Manager or application downloads. ETW traces: the BITS client, BITS server and Drizzle/QMgr providers (NET_BITS). At start and stop TSS saves bitsadmin output (all users' jobs in verbose mode, version, peers) and the network connection profiles (Get-NetConnectionProfile); at stop it adds the Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational event log, the HTTP URL reservations (netsh http show urlacl) and the NLA/NCSI registry keys. With -Mode Restart (or _BITSLOG_RESTART=$True in tss_config.cfg) TSS enables verbose BITS.log logging in the registry and restarts the BITS service at start (not with -noRestart); at stop it copies the BITS log files (System32\bits.*), resets the logging values and restarts BITS again. If _BITSLOG_RESET=$True is set in tss_config.cfg, all BITS jobs of all users are deleted (bitsadmin /Reset /AllUsers) after start. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_Bluetooth
scenarios.description: Use when Bluetooth devices fail to pair, connect or work reliably (for example headsets, keyboards, mice or Bluetooth LE devices). ETW traces: about 55 Bluetooth stack providers such as bthport, bthusb, bthmini, the Bluetooth enumerator and BTHPRINT (NET_Bluetooth). At start TSS turns on verbose logging for the BTHUSB and BTHPort drivers and Secure Simple Pairing debug mode (registry values VerboseOn and SimplePairingDebugEnabled) and enables the Bluetooth-Policy Operational event log. At stop it deletes these registry values again, restores the event log setting and collects the Bluetooth-BthLEPrepairing, Bluetooth-MTPEnum and Bluetooth-Policy Operational event logs, the Bluetooth registry keys (BTHUSB and BTHPort parameters, PolicyManager device policies) and the Bluetooth radio details from scripts\tss_GetBluetoothRadioInfo.ps1 (MAC address, driver version, LE role, secure connections and other radio capabilities). Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_BranchCache
scenarios.description: Use when BranchCache (distributed or hosted cache mode) does not cache or serve content as expected, for example clients still download everything over the WAN. ETW traces: BranchCache (NET_BranchCache), BITS (NET_BITS), Windows Firewall (NET_Firewall), Group Policy (ADS_GPO) and Schannel TLS (ADS_SSL). At start TSS enables the BranchCache analytic event logs and restarts the PeerDistSvc service (-noRestart skips this but enlarges ConfigMgr client logging and copies CCM\Logs at stop). It also enables firewall logging of allowed and dropped connections (pfirewall.log), Filtering Platform auditing (restored at stop), Group Policy debug logging and the CAPI2 log. At start and stop it saves netsh branchcache and Get-BC* status, PeerDist store listings and bitsadmin jobs. At stop: the BranchCache, BITS, firewall, Group Policy, CAPI2 and Security event logs plus Schannel events; BranchCache, TCP/IP, NLA, firewall, Group Policy and TLS registry keys; certificate stores; gpresult; HTTP URL reservations; firewall/IPsec rules, pfirewall.log and netsh wfp show state and filters; the Group Policy debug log files. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Performance Monitor counters of the BC set (CPU, memory, disk, SMB, network and BranchCache) every 10 seconds, Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_Capture
scenarios.description: Use when you only need a network packet capture of the problem without any component ETW tracing, for example to see which packets are sent, received or lost during a failing connection. Tools: a plain netsh packet capture (netsh trace start capture=yes, no netsh scenario providers) written to Netsh_packetcapture.etl as a circular file of 2048 MB by default (-NetshMaxSizeMB changes the size, -NetshOptions adds options such as capture filters), PSR screenshots and a screen video. There are no component traces, common tasks or scenario hooks. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog), so TSS collects no event logs or system information outside the SDP. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_Container
scenarios.description: Use when Windows containers or Kubernetes pods on a Windows host have networking problems, for example no connectivity, DNS or NAT failures, or broken HNS networks and endpoints. ETW traces: the Host Networking Service (NET_HNS), the Hyper-V virtual switch (NET_VMswitch), the Windows Filtering Platform and BFE (NET_WFP, which also enables the WFP Operational event log at start), Windows NAT (NET_WinNAT) and container networking providers such as the HNS overlay plugin, Hyper-V Compute, the VFP extension, NAT and the TCP/IP, DNS and DHCP clients (NET_Container). At stop TSS collects the HNS, Containers-Wcifs/Wcnfs, Hyper-V-Compute, WFP and Firewall event logs, the HNS and vmsmp registry keys, Get-HNSNetwork and Get-HNSEndpoint output (JSON), firewall rules and profiles, network connection profiles, pfirewall.log (if present) and netsh wfp show filters, state, netevents and boot-time policy. With -Mode Docker it adds docker version, info, images, networks (with inspect), running containers (docker inspect), IP addresses of all compartments and Docker Application events of the last 30 minutes; with -Mode Kube it adds kubectl get pods (all namespaces), nodes and services. In every mode TSS also downloads collectlogs.ps1 from the microsoft/SDN GitHub repository and starts it in the background with output to the CollectLogs subfolder (needs Internet access; TSS does not wait for it). Tools: a netsh trace with the Virtualization scenario and capturetype=both (packet capture of physical and virtual switch traffic plus the scenario's ETW providers). There is no PSR or video. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_CSC
scenarios.description: Use when Offline Files (Client-Side Caching, CSC) misbehave, for example files do not synchronize, shares stay offline or the offline cache is slow or corrupt. ETW traces: the SMB client stack with the redirectors, MUP, DFS client, Offline Files kernel and user-mode, WebDAV, Kerberos/NTLM, DNS, NetBT, TCP and QUIC providers (NET_SMBcli). The Offline Files component (NET_CSC) has no ETW providers and only collects data: at start TSS enables the Offline Files Operational, Analytic, Debug and SyncLog event logs and dumps the Offline Files database (cscDBdump.exe dump, skipped in TSS Lite), and again at stop. On builds newer than 17763 NET_SMBcli also enables the SMB client diagnostic, SMB witness and SMBDirect logs. At stop TSS collects all these logs plus the SMBClient Connectivity, Operational and Security logs, the Offline Files (NetCache, CSC, CscService), RPC, TCP/IP, Defender ATP status, LSA and Multimedia SystemProfile registry keys, a few UNC/logon related values (Netlogon, MUP DisableDfs, LmCompatibilityLevel), gpresult and the certificate stores. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Performance Monitor counters of the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB) every 10 seconds, Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DAcli
scenarios.description: Use when a DirectAccess client cannot reach the corporate network or shows a wrong connectivity status, for example IP-HTTPS, Teredo, IPsec or NRPT name resolution failures. ETW traces: IP Helper, which hosts the IPv6 transition tunnels (NET_DAcli), CryptoAPI 2 (NET_CAPI), the DNS client (NET_DNScli), the Network Connectivity Assistant (NET_NCA), WFP and BFE (NET_WFP) and Schannel TLS (ADS_SSL). At start TSS enables the Ncasvc, NCSI, DNS-Client, WFP and CAPI2 event logs; at start and stop it saves netsh output for the IPv6 transition tunnels (6to4, Teredo, IP-HTTPS, ISATAP), the NRPT and the IPsec security associations. At stop it runs scripts\tss_DAclient-collector.ps1 (NCA probe and DTE tests, IP, tunnel, NRPT, NCSI, IPsec and DirectAccess status, certificates, whoami /all), DirectAccess and IPv6 cmdlets (Get-DAConnectionStatus, Get-DnsClientNrptPolicy and more), netsh wfp show state and filters, the DNS client state and gpresult, plus these event logs, the Firewall log, Schannel events and the authentication, cryptography, TLS and WinHTTP registry keys; NET_DNScli also pings two public web sites as stop markers. Tools: a netsh trace with the DirectAccess, WFP-IPsec and NetConnection scenarios (packet capture plus their ETW providers), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DAsrv
scenarios.description: Use on a DirectAccess (Remote Access) server when clients cannot connect through it or DirectAccess configuration or monitoring fails. ETW traces: NDIS (NET_NDIS), Netlogon (NET_Netlogon), the Remote Access server (NET_DAsrv), IP Helper (NET_DAcli), DirectAccess and RaMgmtSvc management (NET_DAmgmt, NET_RAmgmt), WMI (UEX_WMIAdvanced), WinRM (UEX_WinRMBase), LDAP client (ADS_LDAPcli), Schannel (ADS_SSL), WFP (NET_WFP) and Windows NAT (NET_WinNAT). At start TSS enables Netlogon, RaMgmtSvc and svchost.exe LDAP client debug logging and the NCA, NCSI, WFP and CAPI2 logs, saves netsh IPv6 tunnel, NRPT and IPsec SA output and Get-DAEntryPointDC, and on builds up to 17763 with RemoteAccess running disables IPv4 multicast forwarding until stop. Unless -noRestart is used it offers a RaMgmtSvc restart (30 s prompt, default No; clients drop for about 60 s). At stop: netsh ras dump, IP-HTTPS state, Get-DAServer, Get-RemoteAccess and Get-RemoteAccessHealth, the DA client collector script, netsh wfp show, the Remote Access, VPN, NCA, NCSI, WFP, Firewall, CAPI2 and Security event logs, %windir%\debug (netlogon.log), %windir%\tracing (RaMgmtSvc), the WMI-Collect.ps1 and WinRM-Collect.ps1 logs, gpresult and the DirectAccess, LDAP and TLS registry keys. Tools: a netsh trace with the DirectAccess and WFP-IPsec scenarios (packet capture plus their ETW providers), RAS diagnostic tracing (RASdiag), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor and PSR screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DFScli
scenarios.description: Use when a client cannot resolve or open DFS namespace paths (\\domain\namespace), for example missing, wrong or slow referrals or failover to an unexpected target. NET_DFScli uses exactly the same definition as NET_SMBcli, because the DFS client runs inside the SMB client stack. ETW traces: the SMB client stack with the DFS client (dfsc), MUP, redirectors, Offline Files, WebDAV, Kerberos/NTLM, DNS, NetBT, TCP and QUIC providers (NET_SMBcli). On builds newer than 17763 TSS enables the SMB client diagnostic, SMB witness and SMBDirect event logs at start. At stop it collects these logs plus the SMBClient Connectivity, Operational and Security logs, the Offline Files, RPC, TCP/IP, Defender ATP status, LSA and Multimedia SystemProfile registry keys, a few UNC/logon related values (Netlogon, MUP DisableDfs, LmCompatibilityLevel), gpresult and the certificate stores. The NET common tasks also save the DFS referral, domain and MUP caches (DFSutil /PKTinfo, /SPCinfo, /displayMupCache) at start, before the referral cache is flushed, and again at stop. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Performance Monitor counters of the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB) every 10 seconds, Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DFSsrv
scenarios.description: Use on a DFS Namespace (DFS-N) root server when clients get no, wrong or slow referrals or namespace roots and links fail. ETW traces: the SMB server stack including DFS-N, NFS server, Kerberos/NTLM and QUIC providers (NET_SMBsrv) and the DFS Namespace server, filter and DfsSvc providers (NET_DFSsrv). At start TSS saves the open SMB files (Get-SmbOpenFile) and, on builds newer than 17763, enables the SMB server Audit, SMBDirect and analytic event logs. At stop it collects the SMBServer Connectivity, Operational and Security logs (plus Audit and SMBDirect on newer builds, but not the analytic logs), the DFSN-Server logs, the SMB server, DFS, RPC, Defender ATP status and LSA registry keys, gpresult, an SMB server binding check and the share permissions (AccessChk). If the DFS Namespace role is installed it also exports the namespace root with DFSutil and the DFSRoots folder permissions, prompting for the DFSRoots path or the root name when they cannot be determined. With -Mode Permission it asks for a share folder and file and saves their permissions (icacls, AccessChk). AccessChk and DFSutil are skipped in TSS Lite. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Performance Monitor counters of the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB) every 10 seconds, Process Monitor and PSR screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. For the long-running DFSdiag checks use -StartDiag NET_dfsn.

scenarios.name: NET_DHCPcli
scenarios.description: Use when a client cannot obtain, renew or keep an IP address from DHCP (DHCPv4 or DHCPv6), for example it falls back to an APIPA 169.254.x.x address, lease renewals fail or it receives wrong DHCP options. ETW traces: the DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 client, DNS resolver and Winsock name resolution providers (NET_DHCPcli) and the DNS client (NET_DNScli). At start TSS enables the DHCP-Client Operational and Admin, Dhcpv6-Client Operational and DNS-Client Operational event logs; at start and stop it saves the DHCP lease obtained/expires times of each adapter and the DHCP client (Services\Dhcp) and TCP/IP registry keys. Just before the traces stop NET_DNScli pings www.microsoft.de and www.google.de as markers. At stop TSS collects these event logs, the DNS client settings and server addresses (Get-DnsClientGlobalSetting, Get-DnsClientServerAddress, netsh dnsclient show state), netsh wfp show state, filters, netevents and boot-time policy and the authentication, cryptography, TLS, WinHTTP auto-proxy and .NET registry keys. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DHCPsrv
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows DHCP server for lease, scope, option, failover or DNS-update problems. ETW traces: the DHCP Server service and its ESE database (NET_DHCPsrv, plus DhcpServerTrace on build 9600 and later) and the DNS client and resolver (NET_DNScli). At stop TSS collects netsh dhcp show server and about 20 netsh dhcp server show outputs (scopes, options, classes, bindings, audit and DNS settings), Get-DhcpServer* server, database and DNS update settings, the DHCP audit logs (DHCP*.log), DhcpCfg and the backup database (backup\new\dhcp.mdb), AccessChk permissions of these folders (not in Lite mode) and the Dhcp-Server Operational, FilterNotifications and DhcpAdminEvents event logs. NET_DNScli adds the DNS-Client/Operational log (enabled at start), ping markers to www.microsoft.de and www.google.de after the repro, the DNS client settings (Get-DnsClient*, netsh dnsclient show state) and authentication, crypto, TLS, WinHTTP and .NET registry keys. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), PerfMon NET counters (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network) every 10 seconds, Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DNScli
scenarios.description: Use for DNS name resolution problems on a client or server, and when a machine cannot find a domain controller or picks the wrong one (DC Locator). ETW traces: the DNS client, resolver and DNSAPI (NET_DNScli) and the DC Locator with Netlogon/NetLib (NET_DCLocator). At start TSS enables the Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Client/Operational event log; after the repro it pings www.microsoft.de and www.google.de once as trace markers; at stop it collects the DNS client configuration (Get-DnsClientGlobalSetting, Get-DnsClientServerAddress, netsh dnsclient show state), the authentication (Lsa, Kerberos, Netlogon, Winlogon), crypto, TLS, WinHTTP and .NET Framework registry keys and the DNS-Client/Operational log. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_DNSsrv
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows DNS server for zone, record, recursion, forwarding, zone transfer or DNS policy problems. ETW traces: the DNS Server service, DNS server trace, Dnscmd, PowerShell and DNSAPI providers (NET_DNSsrv). At stop TSS exports the DNS Server and Microsoft-Windows-DNSServer/Audit event logs and, if the DNS service exists, collects Dnscmd /Info, /EnumDirectoryPartitions, /EnumZones and /Statistics, 14 Get-DnsServer* outputs (settings, statistics, AD settings, scavenging, recursion, diagnostics, cache, EDNS, forwarders, root hints, zones), the DNS policy configuration (query resolution and zone transfer policies, client subnets, recursion scopes, rate limiting, zone scopes), the DNS Server registry key (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\DNS Server) as a hive plus exports of its Policies, ClientSubnets and Zones keys and the DNS debug log files (%windir%\System32\dns\*.log). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), PerfMon NET counters (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network) every 10 seconds and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. With -Mode Verbose the DNS Server provider is traced with all keywords and the DNS Server WMI provider is added (default: keyword mask 0x3FFE77); nothing else changes.

scenarios.name: NET_Firewall
scenarios.description: Use when Windows Defender Firewall or the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) unexpectedly blocks or allows traffic or rules do not apply. At start TSS enables the firewall, Network Isolation, SENSE and WFP event logs, turns on pfirewall.log logging of dropped and allowed connections, audits Filtering Platform Packet Drop and Connection events (audit policy restored at stop) and enables Group Policy debug logging. At stop it turns that pfirewall.log logging off and collects firewall rules, settings and profiles (Get-NetFirewall*, netsh advfirewall show), pfirewall.log, netsh wfp show state/filters/netevents, firewall registry and BFE key permissions, Defender status, the firewall, WFP, Security and Group Policy event logs, Group Policy debug logs, GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Packet Monitor (PktMon, build 17763 and later only), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_General
scenarios.description: Use for general network problems that do not clearly match a more specific NET_* scenario; if you know the affected technology, use the matching scenario instead. It enables no component ETW traces. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_HypHost
scenarios.description: Use on a Hyper-V host for VM network connectivity problems seen from the host: virtual switch, NIC teaming (LBFO), NAT or host TCP/IP issues. ETW traces: Hyper-V VMBus (SHA_HypVmBus), the Virtual Machine Management Service (SHA_HypVmms), the VM worker process (SHA_HypVmWp), the System Center Virtual Machine Manager debug provider (SHA_VMM), Hyper-V VM configuration (SHA_VmConfig), LBFO NIC teaming with NDIS (NET_LBFO), the NDIS driver layer (NET_NDIS), the Hyper-V virtual switch and its VFP extension (NET_VMswitch), Windows NAT (NET_WinNAT) and Afd/TcpIp/NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop). At stop TSS also collects the LBFO teaming registry keys (Control\Network, NdisImPlatform, MsLbfoProvider) and a listing of the certificate stores and stored credentials (certutil, cmdkey /list). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection and Virtualization scenarios (packet capture plus the scenarios' ETW providers) capturing both physical and virtual switch traffic (capturetype=both, correlation=disabled), a Packet Monitor (PktMon) capture, PerfMon SMB counters (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB) every 10 seconds and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP Cluster report.

scenarios.name: NET_HypVM
scenarios.description: Use inside a Hyper-V virtual machine (guest) for network problems seen in the VM, for example the synthetic network adapter losing connectivity or traffic not reaching the guest. ETW traces: Hyper-V guest networking with the synthetic NIC, NetVSC, NDIS virtual bus and VMBus providers (NET_HypVM) and the NDIS driver layer (NET_NDIS). At start TSS enables the Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-NETVSC/Diagnostic event log and at stop it exports it. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_IIS
scenarios.description: Use on an IIS web server for failing requests, HTTP errors, application pool, site binding or SSL/TLS certificate problems. ETW traces: IIS, WAS, ASP and ASP.NET (NET_IIS), the HTTP.sys kernel driver plus WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_HttpSys), the IIS symbol server proxy (NET_SymProxy) and Schannel and CAPI2 TLS (ADS_SSL). At start TSS saves, clears and enables the Microsoft-Windows-CAPI2/Operational event log and lists the running processes and services. At stop it collects the HTTPERR logs and the inetpub log files, netsh http show servicestate, sslcert and urlacl, appcmd list output (config, worker processes, modules, virtual directories, requests, trace, plus sites, application pools and applications with full configuration) if appcmd.exe exists, the HTTP.sys, TLS (Schannel), WinHTTP and .NET Framework registry keys, the CAPI2/Operational log, the Schannel events of the System log and, if www.ssllabs.com is reachable and the server is not an NPS server, the SSL Labs client test page. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_IPAM
scenarios.description: Use on an IP Address Management (IPAM) server for IPAM problems such as server discovery, data collection tasks or IPAM console and API errors. ETW traces: the Microsoft-Windows-IPAM provider (NET_IPAM). At start TSS enables IPAM debug logging in HKLM\Software\Microsoft\IPAM (EnableLogging plus full IpamServer, IpamApi and Server Manager IPAM plug-in levels), enables the IPAM Admin, Operational, ConfigurationChange, Debug and Analytic event logs and warns not to leave this logging running long term. At stop it deletes these registry values, restores the event log settings, exports the IPAM event logs and copies the IPAM .svclog trace files from the Windows Temp folder, the user's temp folder and the NetworkService profile. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_IPsec
scenarios.description: Use for IPsec problems: IKE/AuthIP negotiation failures, dropped IPsec traffic or connection security rules not applied. ETW traces: the IPsec policy agent and IKEEXT (NET_IPsec), the firewall service, driver and policy (NET_Firewall), Group Policy (ADS_GPO) and WFP with Afd/TcpIp/NetIO (NET_WFP). At start TSS enables success and failure auditing for IPsec Main/Quick/Extended Mode, IPsec Driver, policy change, Other System Events and Filtering Platform Packet Drop/Connection (audit policy restored at stop), the firewall and WFP event logs, pfirewall.log logging of dropped and allowed connections and Group Policy debug logging. At stop it turns that pfirewall.log logging off and collects IPsec rules and state (netsh advfirewall consec/mainmode/monitor, netsh ipsec, Get-NetIPsecRule, Show-NetIPsecRule, Get-NetIPsecMainModeRule), firewall rules and profiles, pfirewall.log, netsh wfp show output, firewall registry, BFE permissions, Defender status, the Security, firewall, WFP and Group Policy event logs, Group Policy debug logs, GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_MBN
scenarios.description: Use for mobile broadband (cellular WWAN/MBN) problems, for example a cellular connection that fails. ETW traces: the WWAN service and cellular stack (NET_MBN), the WmbClass modem driver (NET_WmbClass), Windows Connection Manager (NET_WCM), Radio Manager (NET_RadioManager), the network connection UI (NET_NetworkUX), the DNS client (NET_DNScli), RPC (NET_RPC) and WFP with Afd/TcpIp/NetIO (NET_WFP). At start TSS enables netsh mbn tracing and the DNS-Client and WFP Operational event logs and saves netsh mbn show interfaces/profiles/ready and netsh advfirewall monitor show firewall verbose. At stop it turns mbn tracing off, saves those outputs again and collects the System32\LogFiles\WMI folder, the WwanSvc profiles, the RAS phonebooks (Network\Connections), netcfg -s n, the 802.1X, MBN, TCP, TLS, WinHTTP and RPC registry keys, RPCcfg and RPCdump output (not in Lite mode), the Wcmsvc, WWAN-SVC and Group Policy Operational event logs, the DNS client settings, pfirewall.log and netsh wfp show output. Tools: a netsh trace with the wcn_dbg and wwan_dbg scenarios (packet capture plus their ETW providers), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video.
