Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. -Mode Verbose adds the wireless_dbg netsh scenario.

scenarios.name: NET_Miracast
scenarios.description: Use when projecting to a wireless display with Miracast (Wi-Fi Direct) fails, does not connect or drops. ETW traces: the Miracast source, receiver and logging providers plus the DirectX graphics kernel (NET_Miracast). At stop TSS collects netsh wlan show driver (shows whether the Wi-Fi and graphics drivers support wireless display), the WLAN policies and profiles (wlansvc folders), the 802.1X/WLAN, Miracast (DeviceAssociationService) and firewall registry keys, the firewall rules (Get-NetFirewallRule and related cmdlets), the Group Policy, NetworkProfile, Wired-AutoConfig, Wcmsvc and (on client SKUs) WLAN-AutoConfig Operational logs, the Security log and AuditPol, SecEdit and GPresult output. Tools: a netsh trace (packet capture plus the scenarios' ETW providers) with the WirelessDisplay, wlan_dbg and NetConnection scenarios on build 10586 (Windows 10 1511) and later, or with wlan_dbg and NetConnection on older builds, a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_NCSI
scenarios.description: Use when Windows shows a wrong network connectivity status or network profile, for example a false No Internet access indicator, a domain network detected as Public or Private, or other Network Location Awareness (NLA) problems. ETW traces: NCSI, network status and network icon providers (NET_NCSI) and the Network Profile Manager and Network List Manager (NET_NetProfM). At start TSS enables the NCSI/NLA event logs (NCSI, NlaSvc, NetworkProfile, NetworkLocationWizard, Wired-AutoConfig, Iphlpsvc, GroupPolicy and, on client SKUs, WLAN-AutoConfig) and saves adapter details, network profiles (Get-NetConnectionProfile), the NCSI policy and the DNS NRPT policy; at stop it saves this information again and exports those logs plus the Security and Windows Firewall logs and pfirewall.log, the NlaSvc and NCSI policy registry keys, the proxy configuration (netsh winhttp show proxy, bitsadmin /util /getieproxy, WinHTTPDiag -i, Internet Settings keys), certificate stores and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the wireless_dbg and InternetClient_dbg scenarios plus the PrimaryNetworkIcon and NCSI providers (packet capture plus the scenarios' ETW providers), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_NFScli
scenarios.description: Use when a Windows NFS client (Client for NFS) cannot mount or access NFS exports, or has identity mapping, permission or performance problems. ETW traces: the NFS client redirector and service (NET_NFScli) and the SMB client stack (NET_SMBcli: RDBSS/MUP, SMB and NFS redirectors, Offline Files, DNS, NetBT, Kerberos/NTLM, TCP and QUIC providers). At start, on builds newer than 17763 (Windows Server 2019), TSS enables the SMB client optional and analytic event logs. At stop it exports the NFS client, ONC RPC and Portmapper event logs and the SMB client event logs, and saves the NFS client registry keys (NfsClnt, NfsRdr, Nfsnp, ClientForNFS, ServicesForNFS); if the NfsClnt service exists it saves nfsadmin client and mapping config and mount output, and where the NFS PowerShell cmdlets are installed also Get-NfsClientConfiguration, Get-NfsMappingStore, Test-NfsMappingStore and the mapped identities (Get-NfsMappedIdentity). It also saves Offline Files, RPC, TCP/IP and LSA registry keys, a few UNC hardening values, certificate stores and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB counters every 10 seconds), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_NFSsrv
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows server with the Server for NFS role when NFS clients cannot mount or access its exports, or for identity mapping, permission, locking or performance problems. ETW traces: the NFS server stack (NET_NFSsrv: NFS server, NLM lock manager, NFS filter, ONC RPC/XDR, Portmapper and NFS service providers). At start, if the role is installed, TSS warns when NfsService is not running and sets the NFS server LogActivity to All (Set-NfsServerConfiguration), restoring the previous value before stop. At stop, only on a Server for NFS, it exports the NFS server, ONC RPC and Portmapper event logs and saves the NFS registry keys plus text files with the server configuration and mapping store (Get-NfsServerConfiguration, nfsadmin), mapped identities (Get-NfsMappedIdentity), shares and share permissions (Get-NfsShare, Get-NfsSharePermission, nfsshare, showmount, netgroups, client groups), mounted clients, sessions, locks and open files, and statistics (Get-NfsStatistics, nfsstat). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and PSR screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. With -Mode Permission TSS prompts at stop, without timeout, for an NFS folder and file path (ENTER skips) and saves their permissions (icacls, nfsfile /v and AccessChk) to NFS_permissions_stop_.txt.

scenarios.name: NET_NLB
scenarios.description: Use for Network Load Balancing (NLB) cluster problems, for example convergence failures, hosts leaving the cluster, or client traffic to the cluster IP address that is lost or unevenly distributed. ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop) and NLB (NET_NLB: NLB standard and packet traces, NLB and NLB-Diagnostic events, plus AFD and WFP providers). At start TSS enables the Microsoft-Windows-NLB/Diagnostic event log and saves the ARP table (arp -a); at stop it saves the ARP table again, the NLB cluster state (WLBS display), the WLBS registry key and msinfo32 (.nfo, TSS waits up to 5 minutes for it). Note: the NLB/Diagnostic log is enabled and reset but currently not exported. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_NPS
scenarios.description: Use on a Network Policy Server (NPS/RADIUS) when RADIUS authentication of VPN, Wi-Fi or 802.1X clients fails (rejected requests, EAP, certificate or domain lookup errors). ETW traces: NPS and EAP (NET_NPS), LDAP client calls made by svchost.exe and any -ProcessNames (ADS_LDAPcli), Netlogon (NET_Netlogon), TLS/Schannel and CAPI2 (ADS_SSL) and the Windows Filtering Platform and firewall (NET_WFP). At start TSS runs netsh nps set tracing *=verbose (if the IAS service exists), enables Netlogon debug logging (DbFlag) and LDAP client tracing, saves, clears and enables the CAPI2 Operational log and enables the WFP Operational log. At stop it exports the Security, CAPI2 and WFP logs, Schannel System events and the firewall log with pfirewall.log, and saves netsh wfp show state/filters/netevents/boottimepolicy, netsh nps show config, a netsh nps export (exportPSK=YES, so it contains the RADIUS shared secrets), the System32\LogFiles\NPS and %windir%\debug (netlogon.log) folders, NPS, RAS, LDAP, TLS, WinHTTP and .NET registry keys and certificate stores; it turns NPS tracing off and sets DbFlag to 0. Tools: RASdiag (netsh ras diagnostics tracing plus Network Policy Server success/failure auditing; copies %windir%\tracing at stop), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario plus one extra provider by GUID (packet capture plus ETW providers) and PSR screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_Proxy
scenarios.description: Use when applications or services cannot reach web sites or cloud services through a proxy, for example wrong WinHTTP or WinINet proxy settings, proxy auto-detection or proxy authentication failures. ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop), the NDIS layer (NET_NDIS), WebIO, WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_WebIO), Winsock and name resolution (NET_Winsock) and the network connectivity status indicator (NET_NCSI). At start TSS enables the Microsoft-Windows-WebIO/Diagnostic log and the NCSI/NLA event logs and saves adapter, network profile, NCSI policy and DNS NRPT information; at stop it saves that information again and exports those logs plus the Security and Windows Firewall logs and pfirewall.log, the proxy configuration (netsh winhttp show proxy, bitsadmin /util /getieproxy, WinHTTPDiag -i and the Internet Settings registry keys), the HTTP URL reservations (netsh http show urlacl), NlaSvc/NCSI registry keys, certificate stores and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the wireless_dbg and InternetClient_dbg scenarios plus the PrimaryNetworkIcon provider (packet capture plus the scenarios' ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_RAS
scenarios.description: Use on a Routing and Remote Access (RRAS) VPN server when VPN clients cannot connect or authenticate, connections drop, or the Remote Access service hangs. ETW traces: TLS/Schannel and CAPI2 (ADS_SSL) and the Windows Filtering Platform and firewall (NET_WFP). At start TSS clears the CAPI2 Operational log after saving it, enables it and the WFP Operational log; at stop it exports both logs, Schannel events from the System log, the Windows Firewall log and pfirewall.log, saves netsh wfp show state/filters/netevents/boottimepolicy and the TLS, WinHTTP and .NET registry keys, and, if www.ssllabs.com is reachable and NPS (IAS) is not installed, a TLS client test page. Tools: RASdiag (netsh ras diagnostics tracing plus Network Policy Server success/failure auditing; copies %windir%\tracing at stop), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), a netsh trace with the VpnServer scenario plus one extra provider by GUID (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the NET set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB and network counters every 10 seconds) and PSR screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. With -Mode Hang TSS also creates ProcDump user dumps of RaMgmtui.exe and the Rasman, RemoteAccess, RaMgmtSvc, IKEEXT and BFE services at start and at stop, each time 3 dumps 50 seconds apart.

scenarios.name: NET_RDMA
scenarios.description: Use for SMB Direct (SMB over RDMA) problems, for example RDMA not being used, SMB Direct connections failing, or poor throughput between servers with RDMA network adapters. ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop), the NDIS layer (NET_NDIS), RDMA (NET_RDMA), SMB Direct (NET_SmbCA) and the SMB client stack (NET_SMBcli: redirector, Offline Files, DNS, NetBT, Kerberos/NTLM, TCP and QUIC providers). At start, on builds newer than 17763 (Windows Server 2019), TSS enables the SMB client optional and analytic event logs (including SMBDirect/Admin); at stop it saves the RDMA connection list (netstat -xan), exports the SMB client event logs and saves Offline Files, RPC, TCP/IP and LSA registry keys, a few UNC hardening values, certificate stores and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters every 10 seconds), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_RPC
scenarios.description: Use for RPC or DCOM communication problems, for example RPC server unavailable (error 1722) failures, endpoint mapper or dynamic RPC port problems, or remote COM/DCOM calls that fail or hang. ETW traces: the RPC runtime, RpcSs, endpoint and service trigger, RPC proxy and RPC firewall manager providers (NET_RPC) and COM/OLE32 (NET_OLE32). At stop TSS saves the RPC registry keys (Software\Microsoft\Rpc, RpcSs, RpcEptMapper, RpcLocator and the RPC policy key) and, except in the TSS Lite package, RPCcfg.exe /l and /q output (RPC-config_Stop_.txt) and RPCdump.exe /v /i output with the endpoint mapper registrations (RPC-dump_Stop_.txt). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_SMB
scenarios.description: Use for SMB file sharing problems when you need SMB client and server data from one machine (for example a server that also accesses shares). ETW traces: the SMB client (NET_SMBcli: redirector, Offline Files, DNS, NetBT, Kerberos/NTLM, TCP, QUIC) and the SMB server (NET_SMBsrv: srv/srv2/srvnet, witness, DFS-N, BranchCache hash, NFS server, Storage Replica, Kerberos/NTLM, QUIC). At start TSS saves the open files (Get-SmbOpenFile) and, on builds newer than 17763 (Windows Server 2019), enables the optional and analytic SMB event logs. At stop it exports the SMB client and server event logs (on newer builds plus the optional and client analytic logs) and saves the LanmanServer binding check, the permissions of all shares (AccessChk -h), SMB server, Offline Files, RPC, TCP/IP and LSA registry keys, a few UNC hardening values, certificate stores and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB counters every 10 seconds), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. With -Mode Permission TSS asks at stop whether to collect permissions (30 second timeout, default No), then prompts for a local share folder and file and saves their icacls and AccessChk output to SMB_permissions_stop_.txt (skipped in the TSS Lite package).

scenarios.name: NET_SMBcli
scenarios.description: Use on the client side when access to SMB file shares fails or is slow, for example access denied, disconnects, slow file copies, mapped drive, DFS or Offline Files problems. ETW traces: the SMB client stack (NET_SMBcli: RDBSS, MUP and DFS client, MRxSMB/SMB2 redirector and SMB client events, witness client, Offline Files, BranchCache, WebDAV client, folder redirection, NetBT, DNS client, NFS redirector, Kerberos, NTLM, NegoExts and PKU2U, TCP and QUIC providers). At start, on builds newer than 17763 (Windows Server 2019), TSS enables the SMB client optional and analytic event logs (SMBWitnessClient, SMBDirect/Admin, SMBClient Audit, Diagnostic, HelperClassDiagnostic and ObjectStateDiagnostic). At stop it exports the SMBClient Connectivity, Operational and Security logs (plus the logs enabled at start) and saves Offline Files (NetCache, CSC), RPC, TCP/IP, Defender ATP, LSA and Multimedia SystemProfile registry keys, a few UNC hardening related values (Reg_UNChard1.txt), certificate stores (certutil, cmdkey /list) and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_SMBsrv
scenarios.description: Use on a file server when clients cannot access its SMB shares or access is slow (access denied, disconnects, permission problems). ETW traces: the SMB server stack (NET_SMBsrv: srv/srv2/srvnet, SMB server events, witness, BranchCache hash, DFS-N filter, NFS server, Storage Replica, Kerberos/NTLM and QUIC providers). At start TSS saves the open files (Get-SmbOpenFile) and, on builds newer than 17763 (Windows Server 2019), enables the SMBServer Audit, SMBDirect/Admin and analytic logs. At stop it exports the SMBServer Connectivity, Operational and Security logs (plus Audit and SMBDirect/Admin on newer builds; the analytic logs are not exported) and saves the LanmanServer binding check, the permissions of all shares (AccessChk -h, not in the TSS Lite package), the SMB server and LSA registry keys and GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), a Performance Monitor counter log with the SMB set (CPU, memory, disk, process and SMB counters every 10 seconds) and PSR screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. With -Mode Permission TSS asks at stop whether to collect permissions (30 second timeout, default No), then prompts for a local share folder and file and saves their icacls and AccessChk output to SMB_permissions_stop_.txt (also skipped in the TSS Lite package).

scenarios.name: NET_SQLtrace
scenarios.description: Use for SQL Server connectivity problems (for example connection timeouts, login or network errors between a SQL client and the SQL server) when you need a network capture together with SQL performance counters. No component ETW traces are enabled. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and a Performance Monitor counter log with the SQL set (General, SMB, NET and SQL Server counters, every 10 seconds unless -PerfIntervalSec). Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP SQLbase report (SQL Server logs, minidumps and configuration checks plus TCP/IP, DNS client, firewall and cluster information).

scenarios.name: NET_TestMe
scenarios.description: Internal test scenario used by TSS developers to check the framework itself (scenario start and stop flow and the scenario hook calls); do not use it for customer data collection. No component ETW traces are enabled. Tools: a plain netsh packet capture (Netsh, capture only, no netsh scenario providers). The scenario hooks collect nothing; they only print test messages when the hidden -beta switch is used. There is no NET common task, so at stop TSS only adds the default basic log (skip it with -noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: NET_UNChard
scenarios.description: Use when SYSVOL or NETLOGON (hardened UNC paths) cannot be reached or are slow at startup or logon, for example Group Policy or logon script failures related to the Hardened UNC Paths policy. ETW traces: the SMB client (NET_SMBcli), DC Locator (NET_DCLocator), Netlogon (NET_Netlogon), Winlogon (NET_Winlogon), Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel and LSA authentication (ADS_Auth), the User Profile Service (ADS_Profile) and Group Policy (ADS_GPO); ADS_GPsvc adds no ETW providers, only GPSvc and Netlogon debug logging. At start TSS turns on Netlogon, LSA/Kerberos and Group Policy (Preferences, Administrative Templates, security CSE) debug logging and enables about 30 authentication, SMB client and profile event logs. At stop it reverts these settings and collects %windir%\debug (netlogon.log, GPSvc.log), the SMB client, Group Policy, profile and authentication event logs, GPresult, certificate stores, CSC, SMB, TCP, TLS and LSA registry keys, the HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft tree (holds the HardenedPaths policy) and UNC hardening related values (Reg_UNChard1.txt). Tools: Process Monitor, a plain netsh packet capture, PerfMon SMB counters (General and SMB, every 10 seconds), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. For boot traces (-StartAutoLogger) TSS reminds you to wait up to 4 minutes after the reboot, then log on with the same user and run -StopAutoLogger.

scenarios.name: NET_VPN
scenarios.description: Use for VPN client problems (Always On VPN, IKEv2, SSTP or plug-in VPN connections that fail to connect, authenticate or stay up). ETW traces: IPsec (NET_IPsec), the network flyout UI (NET_NetworkUX), the VPN client, plug-in platform, EAP and IKE stack (NET_VPN) and the Windows Filtering Platform (NET_WFP). At start TSS enables IPsec, filtering platform and NPS security auditing and the RasAgileVpn, CAPI2 (cleared) and WFP event logs. At stop it collects the Security, CAPI2, DNS client, VPN, RasAgileVpn, WFP and firewall event logs, IPsec rules (netsh and Get-NetIPsecRule), netsh wfp show state, filters and netevents, pfirewall.log, the .pbk phone books, the MDM VPN profile XMLs read as the user and as SYSTEM (scripts\tss_ExportVPNProfiles.ps1), Get-VpnConnection and NRPT rules, Credential Guard state, Azure VPN client logs, certificate stores and proxy settings. Tools: RAS diagnostic tracing (RASdiag, copies %windir%\tracing), a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots, a screen video and a netsh trace (packet capture plus scenario providers) with the VpnClient_dbg scenario on build 17763 and later (VpnClient with -Mode Basic) or InternetClient_dbg on older builds, each plus the RAS NdisWan packet capture provider (traffic inside the tunnel) and one more provider. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_WebClient
scenarios.description: Use when WebDAV access through the WebClient service fails, prompts or is slow, for example SharePoint Explorer view or drives mapped to http(s) web folders. ETW traces: the WebDAV, RDBSS, MUP and SMB client redirectors (NET_WebClient), SSL/TLS Schannel (ADS_SSL) and WebIO, WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_WebIO). At start TSS enables the CAPI2 (cleared) and WebIO diagnostic event logs and asks you to keep only one browser window or tab and one Explorer window open. At stop it collects the CAPI2 and WebIO logs, Schannel events, proxy settings (netsh winhttp, WinHTTPDiag), HTTP URL reservations (netsh http show urlacl), WebClient, MRxDAV, Internet Settings, TLS and .NET registry keys, GPresult and a TLS test page from www.ssllabs.com; if the WebClient service is running it then prompts (input box, may be hidden behind other windows) for the URL of the target web folder and runs scripts\tss_MSDavConnection.ps1 to test WebDAV settings and connectivity. Tools: a netsh trace (packet capture plus scenario providers) with the InternetClient_dbg scenario plus the Microsoft-Windows-WinHttp and Microsoft-Windows-WebIO providers at level=5, Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. -Mode Restart restarts the WebClient service after the traces have started and moves it into its own svchost process (sc config type= own, not reverted at stop).

scenarios.name: NET_WebCliTTD
scenarios.description: Deprecated: use NET_WebClient instead. Collects the same data as NET_WebClient for WebDAV/WebClient problems. It also requests a Time Travel Debugging (TTD) recording of the Explorer, iexplore and msedge processes and of the WebClient service that are running when TSS starts, but in the current code this process list does not reach the TTD start step (it only reads the -TTD command-line value), so no TTD recording is made; TSS still needs TSS_TTD.zip or the UWP TTD app and exits at start when neither is installed. To record WebClient with TTD, run NET_WebClient and add -TTD with the process or service name. ETW traces: the WebDAV, RDBSS, MUP and SMB client redirectors (NET_WebClient), SSL/TLS Schannel (ADS_SSL) and WebIO, WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_WebIO). At stop it collects the CAPI2 and WebIO diagnostic event logs, Schannel events, proxy settings, HTTP URL reservations (netsh http show urlacl), WebClient, MRxDAV, Internet Settings, TLS and .NET registry keys, GPresult and a TLS test page; if the WebClient service is running it prompts for the target web folder URL and runs scripts\tss_MSDavConnection.ps1 (this collection runs twice here, so the prompt can appear twice). Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario plus the Microsoft-Windows-WinHttp and Microsoft-Windows-WebIO providers at level=5, Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. -Mode Restart restarts the WebClient service in its own svchost after the traces have started.

scenarios.name: NET_WebIO
scenarios.description: Use when an application or service fails to make HTTP/HTTPS calls through the Windows web client stacks WinINet, WinHTTP or WebIO (for example proxy, authentication or connection errors). ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop), the NDIS network driver layer (NET_NDIS) and WebIO, WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_WebIO). At start TSS enables the Microsoft-Windows-WebIO/Diagnostic event log; at stop it exports it and collects the proxy configuration (netsh winhttp show proxy, bitsadmin /util /getieproxy for the service accounts, WinHTTPDiag -i and the Internet Settings registry keys) and the HTTP URL reservations (netsh http show urlacl). Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_WFP
scenarios.description: Use for Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) problems, the packet filtering engine under Windows Firewall and IPsec: connections silently blocked or dropped, third-party filter or callout drivers interfering, or Base Filtering Engine (BFE) service failures. ETW traces: the Base Filtering Engine and firewall policy (NET_BFE), IPsec (NET_IPsec) and WFP with its kernel and user-mode clients plus Afd, TCP/IP and NetIO (NET_WFP). At start TSS enables IPsec and filtering platform security auditing (including packet drops) and the WFP operational event log. At stop it restores the audit policy and collects the Security, WFP and firewall event logs, netsh wfp show netevents, state, filters and boottimepolicy (XML), pfirewall.log, IPsec rules (netsh and Get-NetIPsecRule) and the BFE registry permissions. Tools: a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag, netsh wfp capture into WFPdiag.cab), a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_Winsock
scenarios.description: Use when applications fail to create, connect or use sockets, or Winsock name resolution fails, for example after a third-party Layered Service Provider or namespace provider was installed. ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop), the NDIS network driver layer (NET_NDIS) and the Winsock sockets, helper and name resolution providers (NET_Winsock). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_WIP
scenarios.description: Use for Windows Information Protection (WIP, formerly EDP) problems: apps or files classified wrongly as enterprise or personal, blocked access to work resources, or WIP policy not applied. ETW traces: AppLocker and AppID (UEX_AppLocker), Windows Defender Firewall (NET_Firewall), Group Policy (ADS_GPO), the Windows Filtering Platform (NET_WFP) and the AppID logger (NET_WIP). NET_WIP also runs a WPR trace with the EDP profile (config\WIP_WprProfile.xml) and saves WIP packages in EdpDiagnostics at start and stop: AppLocker policy files, EFS, EDP and MDM registry, EDP and device management event logs, MdmDiagnosticsTool output, EDP configuration (scripts\WIP_EDPconfig.ps1), NGC and certificate enrollment debug data, SMB client logs and RAS tracing. TSS also turns on firewall logging (pfirewall.log), packet drop and connection auditing and Group Policy debug logging; at stop it adds firewall rules and state, netsh wfp show output, the AppLocker effective policy, firewall, WFP, AppLocker and Group Policy event logs, GPresult, Defender status and the Security log. Tools: a WFP diagnostic capture (WFPdiag), a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. Side effect: the Windows Biometric service is stopped at start.

scenarios.name: NET_WLAN
scenarios.description: Use for Wi-Fi connect, roaming, disconnect or 802.1X/EAP authentication problems (same definition as NET_802Dot1x). ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, with TCP rundown and port exhaustion checks), NDIS (NET_NDIS), the Radio Manager and airplane mode (NET_RadioManager), SSL/TLS Schannel (ADS_SSL), the Windows Connection Manager (NET_WCM) and the network flyout UI (NET_NetworkUX). At start and stop TSS saves netsh wlan show output, a WLAN report and the WLAN profiles (netsh wlan export profile, keys encrypted); at start it also clears the CAPI2 event log, and on Surface devices with the Marvell Wi-Fi driver it sets debug registry keys (a reboot is needed the first time; removed at stop). At stop it collects the Group Policy, NetworkProfile, Wired-AutoConfig, Wcmsvc, CAPI2 and Security event logs, Schannel events, 802.1X, TLS, WinHTTP and .NET registry keys, the wlansvc policies and profiles, dot3svc policy files, .pbk phone books, wlan-report-latest.html (build 16299+), certificate stores, Credential Guard state and driverquery output. Tools: a netsh trace with the dot3_wpp and wireless_dbg scenarios (global level 0xff) plus the CAPI2, EapHost and two more providers (packet capture plus the scenario providers), RAS diagnostic tracing (RASdiag), Process Monitor, PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_WNV
scenarios.description: Use on Hyper-V hosts for Windows Network Virtualization and SDN problems, for example VMs that cannot reach each other across virtual networks, or NIC teaming and virtual switch issues. ETW traces: the TCP/IP stack with Afd, TcpIp and NetIO (NET_AfdTcpFull, which also runs a TCP connection rundown at start and stop and a TCP/UDP port exhaustion check at stop), LBFO NIC teaming with NDIS (NET_LBFO), the SDN Network Controller host agent (NET_NCHA) and the Hyper-V virtual switch with VFP (NET_VMswitch). At stop TSS collects the LBFO related registry keys (Control\Network, NdisImPlatform, MsLbfoProvider) and a full certificate store dump (certutil). Tools: a netsh trace with the Virtualization and InternetClient scenarios (packet capture plus the scenarios' ETW providers) that captures on physical and virtual switch ports (capturetype=both) and at multiple layers (captureMultilayer=yes), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: NET_WorkFolders
scenarios.description: Use for Work Folders sync problems on a client or on the Work Folders (Sync Share) server. ETW traces: Work Folders, its ESE metadata store and Cloud Files (NET_Workfolders) and HTTP.sys with WinHTTP and WinINet (NET_HttpSys). At start TSS enables the Work Folders debug and analytic event logs (client OS) or the SyncShare debug log (server OS), clears the CAPI2 log and runs scripts\tss_WorkFoldersDiag.ps1 (OS, volume and binary version info). At stop it collects the Work Folders Operational, ManagementAgent, Debug and Analytic logs (client OS) or the SyncShare Operational and Reporting logs and HTTPERR logs (server OS), the CAPI2 log and HTTP URL reservations (netsh http show urlacl); tss_WorkFoldersDiag.ps1 then zips the Work Folders registry, the sync share configuration and ACLs (server) and recent events into <computer>_WorkFoldersDiagOutput.zip. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor, a PerfMon ALL counter log (General, SMB, NET, SQL, DC and Cluster counters, every 10 seconds), PSR screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. -Mode Advanced also copies the Work Folders metadata (client metadata or each sync share's staging Metadata folder) and therefore stops the Work Folders services (WorkFolderssvc, or SyncShareSvc and SyncShareTTSvc) during the stop phase and restarts them.

scenarios.name: PRF_Boot
scenarios.description: Use for slow boot, slow startup or slow sign-in, or services that start late after a restart. Start it with -StartAutoLogger (.\TSS.ps1 -StartAutoLogger -Scenario PRF_Boot): TSS sets the traces up as boot-time autologgers; restart the computer (Restart, not Shutdown), sign in and reproduce, then run .\TSS.ps1 -Stop. ETW traces: the Local Security Authority, lsass.exe including Netlogon and Credential Manager providers (ADS_LSA), credential providers and the sign-in UI (ADS_CredprovAuthui), Winlogon, the user profile service and the session manager (UEX_Logon) and the Service Control Manager and svchost (PRF_SCM). At start TSS enables Netlogon debug logging (nltest /dbflag:0x2EFFFFFF) and Group Policy service debug logging (GPSvcDebugLevel registry value) and registers an extra boot session (WPR OnOff Collector) with about 15 boot providers (kernel boot, PnP and prefetch, SMSS, services, Winlogon, Group Policy, Task Scheduler, Code Integrity, ReadyBoost). At stop it turns both debug logs off, copies %windir%\debug\UserMode (gpsvc.log) and the netlogon logs, stops that session and merges it with the WPR boot trace into WPR-boottrace-merged.etl (xperf -merge); it also exports the Winlogon, Authentication and Assigned Access (kiosk) registry keys plus Get-AssignedAccess, Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers and Get-StartApps output (LogonLog folder). Tools: a WPR boot trace with the General profile (GeneralProfile, CPU, DiskIO, FileIO, Minifilter, Registry, Network). A reboot is required and the debug logging stays on until -Stop. Without -StartAutoLogger the same traces only run live in the current session and no boot is captured.

scenarios.name: PRF_Clipboard
scenarios.description: Use when copy, cut and paste, clipboard history (Win+V) or cloud clipboard sync fails or misbehaves. ETW traces: the clipboard stack, that is clipboard history UI and service, AppModel and OLE clipboard, cloud clipboard with the Connected Devices Platform and the Remote Desktop clipboard RdpClip (PRF_Clipboard), the Win32k window manager and input layer (UEX_Win32k) and the Windows shell and File Explorer (PRF_Shell). At stop TSS exports the Explorer policy, shell and file association and thumbnail cache registry keys, saves the HKCU and HKLM Explorer keys as hives and copies the ARCache folder and the user and all-users Start Menu Programs shortcuts (ShellLog folder). Tools: a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilter, network and registry activity), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions.

scenarios.name: PRF_Cortana
scenarios.description: Use when Cortana fails to start, respond or search, including problems with the Cortana search box and its Windows Search integration. ETW traces: AppX deployment and app readiness (PRF_AppX), the Cortana app with its speech and web platform providers (PRF_Cortana), the Windows shell and File Explorer (PRF_Shell), COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM) and Windows Search with the indexer and the search client tquery.dll (PRF_Search). At stop TSS collects: AppX package lists for the current and all users and provisioned packages, about 20 AppX, Store and shell event logs, the AppX, AppModel, StateRepository and AppContainer registry, WindowsApps and SystemApps folder listings, Panther logs, the AppRepository .srd database and ARCache (AppXLog folder); the Cortana and Windows Search policy and settings registry (CortanaLog); Explorer policy and association registry, Explorer hives and Start Menu shortcuts (ShellLog); and it runs scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (COM and DCOM registry and security settings, COM+ applications, msinfo32, gpresult, netstat, hotfixes, System and Application event logs, a WMI/RPC/DCOM diagnostic report and process dumps of dllhost.exe and of the svchost processes hosting WinMgmt, RpcSs/DcomLaunch and the COM+ Event System). Tools: a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilter, network and registry), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR). With -EnableCOMDebug TSS also sets ExecutablesToTrace=* under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing for the trace and removes it at stop.

scenarios.name: PRF_General
scenarios.description: Use as a broad first capture for intermittent or complex slowness, hangs or delays that do not fit a more specific scenario. No ETW components are traced; the data comes from tools. Tools: a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilter, network and registry), a Performance Monitor counter log with the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters) sampled every 10 seconds, a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP report: the scenario requests the deprecated SDP type Perf, which in an interactive run falls back to the NET SDP collectors; if the trace is stopped by a separate .\TSS.ps1 -Stop run, TSS instead prints "SDP Perf is deprecated" and exits at the SDP step, so no SDP is built and the results are not zipped.

scenarios.name: PRF_GeoLocation
scenarios.description: Use when Windows shows a wrong location, the automatic time zone does not update, or the location service fails on Wi-Fi or cellular networks. ETW traces: the Windows location stack, that is the Geolocation service (lfsvc), location API and runtime, geofence monitor and automatic time-zone update (PRF_GeoLocation). At start TSS records the visible Wi-Fi networks with their BSSIDs (netsh wlan show network mode=bssid), the WLAN drivers (netsh wlan show drivers) and the physical wireless adapters (Geolocation_wlan_Start_.txt), then deletes the location cache (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\LfSvc\Cache) and restarts the Geolocation service (lfsvc) so the location is resolved fresh during the trace. At stop it tests HTTPS (TCP 443) reachability of the location endpoints inference.location.live.net, location.microsoft.com, geolocation.microsoft.com, geo.prod.do.dsp.mp.microsoft.com and www.bing.com (results in the TSS console log) and exports the location registry (lfsvc settings, LocationAndSensors and AppPrivacy policies, MDM PolicyManager System and Privacy, the location consent store and Edge and Chrome policies) to Reg_GeoLocation_Stop_.txt. Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: PRF_HighCPU
scenarios.description: Use when a process, a service or the whole system shows high CPU usage and you need to know which process, thread and call stack consume it; start the trace, reproduce the CPU spike, then stop soon after. No ETW components are traced. Tools: an Xperf kernel trace with the CPU profile (process and thread activity, image loads, CPU sampling, context switches, ready threads, DPCs and interrupts, dispatcher and power events, with call stacks for samples and context switches), written to Xperf_CPU.etl as a circular buffer of 2048 MB by default (change with -XperfMaxFileMB), so only the most recent activity is kept; plus Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions. Side effect: before Xperf starts TSS sets DisablePagingExecutive=1 under HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management (if it is not already 1) and removes this value again after Xperf stops.

scenarios.name: PRF_LockScreen
scenarios.description: Use when the screen locks unexpectedly or at the wrong time, the lock screen does not appear, or locking and unlocking misbehaves. ETW traces: the lock screen with Winlogon, WinInit, user profile, screen saver, idle detection, immersive shell and Win32k input providers (PRF_LockScreen). At stop TSS runs AuditPol /get /category:*, a SecEdit security policy export and gpresult (/h, /v and /r; computer scope only when TSS runs under a local account) and saves the HKLM\SOFTWARE, HKCU\SOFTWARE and SYSTEM control set registry hives. Tools: an Xperf kernel trace with the LockScreen profile (process and thread activity, image loads, CPU sampling, DPCs and interrupts, dispatcher and context switches with call stacks, plus a Microsoft-Windows-Winlogon event session) written to Xperf_LockScreen.etl, Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Side effect: before Xperf starts TSS sets DisablePagingExecutive=1 under HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management (if it is not already 1) and removes this value again after Xperf stops.

scenarios.name: PRF_MediaCamera
scenarios.description: Use when a camera does not start, shows no picture or fails to capture, or when audio or video playback, casting or media capture fails in Windows or in apps. ETW traces: the media pipeline, that is Media Foundation (platform, pipeline, playback, capture engine, video processor and media engine), DirectShow, DXVA2 video acceleration, audio and video codecs (H.264, HEVC, MPEG-2, WMV), Windows Media Player, audio, PlayReady, media streaming, Miracast casting and Remote Desktop media redirection (PRF_Media), and the camera stack: the Camera app, the Media Foundation capture engine, MediaCapture and Frame Server, kernel streaming, the sensor service and Plug and Play (PRF_Camera). Neither component collects extra data at stop. Tools: Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions.

scenarios.name: PRF_Perflib
scenarios.description: Use when performance counters are missing, corrupt or fail to load (for example in Performance Monitor, typeperf or monitoring agents that use PDH or the WMI Win32_Perf* classes), or when lodctr counter registration fails. ETW traces: the counter stack PDH, loadperf and Perflib plus the WMI performance classes (PRF_Perflib, written to two ETL files, Perflib and WmiPerf), the WMI service at advanced level (UEX_WMIAdvanced; -WMIProvList adds selected WMI provider traces) and COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM). UEX_WMIAdvanced saves the task list (tasklist /svc and /v) at start and stop and, on build 26063 or later, runs a WMI arbitrator task dump (winmgmt /dumptasks arb) in the background. At stop TSS collects a PerflibLog folder (Services key and 64-bit and 32-bit Perflib registry as text, .reg and .hiv, counter help text, perf*.dat files, INF folder listing, typeperf -q/-qx and lodctr /Q output for 64-bit and 32-bit, the Win32_Perf* class list and the System, Application and Diagnosis-PLA/Operational event logs), then runs scripts\Wmi-Collect.ps1 -Logs (WBEM folder listing, WMI, OLE and RPC registry, event subscriptions, provider host and quota details, WMI-Activity event log, a WMI/RPC/DCOM health check and ProcDump dumps of the WMI service host, WmiPrvSE.exe and other WMI host processes) and scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (msinfo32, COM security, COM, COM+ and RPC registry, COM+ applications and dumps of dllhost.exe and the RPC, DCOM and COM+ event system service hosts). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon) and a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk, file, network and registry activity). No PerfMon counter log is recorded and no service is restarted; with -EnableCOMDebug TSS sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and deletes this value at stop.

scenarios.name: PRF_Photo
scenarios.description: Use when the Photos app fails to start, crashes, hangs or cannot open or display images, including when the cause may be app activation, registration or packaging. ETW traces: the Photos app (PRF_Photo), the AppX deployment and app model stack covering deployment, packaging, activation, process lifetime and the State Repository (PRF_AppX), the Windows shell and File Explorer (PRF_Shell) and COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM). At stop TSS collects AppX data (AppXLog folder: Get-AppxPackage for the current and all users, provisioned packages, about 20 event logs including System, Application, AppXDeployment, AppReadiness, StateRepository and Store, the AppX, AppModel, StateRepository and AppContainer registry, the State Repository databases, Panther logs, AppXProvisioning.xml and WindowsApps, SystemApps and Packages folder listings), shell data (ShellLog folder: Explorer policies, file association and thumbnail cache settings, the HKCU and HKLM Explorer keys as hives, the app resolver cache and the Start menu shortcuts) and the output of scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (msinfo32, COM security, COM, COM+ and RPC registry, COM+ applications, System and Application event logs and process dumps of dllhost.exe and the RPC, DCOM and COM+ event system service hosts). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon), a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk, file, network and registry activity) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Per-user data (HKCU and AppData) comes from the account running TSS. With -EnableCOMDebug TSS sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and deletes this value at stop.

scenarios.name: PRF_ScreenSaver
scenarios.description: Use when the screen saver does not start or starts unexpectedly, or the display does not turn off or the device does not sleep after the configured idle timeout (for example because an application or driver keeps a power request active). ETW traces: power management, power requests, power policy, sleep study and energy estimation (DND_Power), the screen saver, lock screen, Winlogon, user profile, input and idle detection providers (PRF_ScreenSaver, same provider list as PRF_LockScreen) and the Desktop Window Manager and DirectX graphics kernel (PRF_DWM). At start TSS saves powercfg /q, /a, /getactivescheme and /requests; during the repro it appends powercfg /requests output to PowerCfg_requests.txt about every second, which shows the processes, services and drivers that block the idle timeout; at stop it saves powercfg /requests again and collects AuditPol, SecEdit and GPresult (/h, /v and /r; computer scope only for a local account; skipped with -noGPresult). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon, 3096 MB ring buffer by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). Component logs are not collected (no CollectComponentLog), so no powercfg energy, battery or sleep study reports are created.

scenarios.name: PRF_Search
scenarios.description: Use when Windows Search returns no or incomplete results, is slow, or the search index does not build or update, for example when searching in File Explorer or from the taskbar or Start. ETW traces: the Windows Search indexer, search core, protocol handlers, profile notification and the search client tquery.dll (PRF_Search) and the Windows shell and File Explorer (PRF_Shell). At stop TSS collects shell data (ShellLog folder): Explorer policies from HKLM and HKCU, file association and thumbnail cache settings, the HKCU and HKLM Explorer keys as hives, the app resolver cache and the user and all-users Start menu shortcuts. No Windows Search configuration, index files or Search event logs are collected. Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon, 3096 MB ring buffer by default), a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilter, network and registry activity) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Per-user data (HKCU and AppData) comes from the account running TSS.

scenarios.name: PRF_StartMenu
scenarios.description: Use when the Start menu does not open, is slow, shows missing, blank or duplicate tiles or app entries, or loses its layout (for example after an upgrade or a profile change). ETW traces: the Start menu experience, tile data model, layout, cloud data store and content delivery providers (PRF_StartMenu), the AppX deployment and app model stack (PRF_AppX), COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM) and the Windows shell and File Explorer (PRF_Shell). At stop TSS collects Start menu data (StartMenuLog folder: tile and unified tile model caches of ShellExperienceHost and StartMenuExperienceHost, decoded with datastorecachedumptool.exe when present, Start UI tracelogging files, the CloudStore and CuratedTileCollections registry, default layout files, ContentDeliveryManager state and registry, application shortcuts, Start menu folders and miglog.xml), AppX data (AppXLog folder: installed and provisioned packages, about 20 event logs including AppXDeployment, AppReadiness, StateRepository, Shell-Core and Store, the AppX, AppModel, StateRepository and AppContainer registry, the State Repository databases, Panther logs and app folder listings), shell data (ShellLog folder: Explorer policies, associations, Explorer hives and Start menu shortcuts) and the output of scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (msinfo32, COM security, COM, COM+ and RPC registry and dumps of dllhost.exe and the RPC, DCOM and COM+ event system service hosts). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon), a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk, file, network and registry activity) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Per-user data (HKCU and AppData) comes from the account running TSS. With -EnableCOMDebug TSS sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and deletes this value at stop.

scenarios.name: PRF_Store
scenarios.description: Use when the Microsoft Store app does not open, cannot search, sign in or license apps, or Store app downloads, installs or updates fail. ETW traces: the Store client, Store agent, licensing, push-to-install and Windows Update client providers plus the Azure AD, Windows Hello (NGC), TPM, certificate enrollment, device management enrollment and WinHTTP providers used for sign-in and licensing (PRF_Store), the AppX deployment and app model stack (PRF_AppX), COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM) and the Windows shell (PRF_Shell). At stop TSS collects AppX data (AppXLog folder: Get-AppxPackage for the current and all users, provisioned packages, about 20 event logs including Store, AppXDeployment, AppReadiness, StateRepository and AAD, the AppX, AppModel, StateRepository and AppContainer registry, the State Repository databases, Panther logs and WindowsApps and Packages folder listings), shell data (ShellLog folder: Explorer policies, associations, Explorer hives, app resolver cache and Start menu shortcuts) and the output of scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (msinfo32, COM security, COM, COM+ and RPC registry and dumps of dllhost.exe and the RPC, DCOM and COM+ event system service hosts). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon), a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk, file, network and registry activity) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Per-user data (HKCU and AppData) comes from the account running TSS. With -EnableCOMDebug TSS sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and deletes this value at stop.

scenarios.name: PRF_UWP
scenarios.description: Use for problems with UWP and other packaged (AppX/MSIX) apps, such as apps that fail to install, update, register, start or activate, crash at launch or disappear, especially when the Start menu or shell integration is also affected. ETW traces: the AppX deployment and app model stack covering deployment, packaging, activation, process lifetime and the State Repository (PRF_AppX), COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM), the Windows shell and File Explorer (PRF_Shell) and the Start menu, tile and layout providers (PRF_StartMenu). At stop TSS collects AppX data (AppXLog folder: Get-AppxPackage for the current and all users, provisioned packages, about 20 event logs including AppXDeployment, AppReadiness, StateRepository, Store and AAD, the AppX, AppModel, StateRepository and AppContainer registry, the State Repository databases, Panther logs and app folder listings), Start menu data (StartMenuLog folder: tile caches, CloudStore registry, default layout, ContentDeliveryManager state and Start menu shortcuts), shell data (ShellLog folder: Explorer policies, associations, Explorer hives and Start menu shortcuts) and the output of scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (msinfo32, COM security, COM, COM+ and RPC registry and dumps of dllhost.exe and the RPC, DCOM and COM+ event system service hosts). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon), a WPR trace with the lighter General_Light profile (CPU, handles and registry plus reduced disk, file, minifilter and network events) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Per-user data (HKCU and AppData) comes from the account running TSS. With -EnableCOMDebug TSS sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and deletes this value at stop.

scenarios.name: PRF_WinGet
scenarios.description: Use when winget (Windows Package Manager, part of App Installer) fails to install, upgrade, list or find packages or sources, including MSIX and Store packages installed through winget. ETW traces: the AppX deployment and app model stack (PRF_AppX), the Start menu, tile and layout providers (PRF_StartMenu), the Store, licensing, Windows Update client, sign-in and certificate providers (PRF_Store) and COM, DCOM, WinRT activation and RPC (UEX_COM). At stop the data-collection-only winget component (PRF_WinGet, no ETW providers) collects winget --info (winget_info.txt), the App Installer diagnostic logs from its DiagOutputDir (WingetLogs folder), the registered Windows Update services (WsServices.txt), an MDM diagnostics report (MdmDiagnosticsTool.exe, DeviceManagement_and_MDM folder) and WindowsUpdate.log (Get-WindowsUpdateLog). TSS also collects AppX data (AppXLog folder: installed and provisioned packages, about 20 event logs including AppXDeployment, AppReadiness, StateRepository and Store, the AppX, AppModel and StateRepository registry, the State Repository databases and app folder listings), Start menu data (StartMenuLog folder: tile caches, CloudStore registry, default layout and Start menu shortcuts) and the output of scripts\COM-Collect.ps1 (msinfo32, COM security, COM, COM+ and RPC registry and dumps of dllhost.exe and the RPC, DCOM and COM+ event system service hosts). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots; there is no WPR trace. Per-user data (winget logs, HKCU and AppData) comes from the account running TSS. With -EnableCOMDebug TSS sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and deletes this value at stop.

scenarios.name: SHA_General
scenarios.description: Use as a catch-all for storage, failover cluster or Hyper-V problems when the failing component is not yet known. The scenario has no ETW components; it gathers generic data with tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, Performance Monitor counters of the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP Cluster report. When the area is known, use SHA_MScluster, SHA_HypHost or SHA_HypVM instead.

scenarios.name: SHA_HypHost
scenarios.description: Run on the Hyper-V host for host-side Hyper-V problems: VMs that fail to start, stop or change state, VMBus or configuration errors, and VM networking or SMB storage problems. ETW traces: VMBus and KMCL (SHA_HypVmBus), the management service vmms.exe (SHA_HypVmms), the VM worker process vmwp.exe (SHA_HypVmWp), the Microsoft-VirtualMachineManager-Debug provider (SHA_VMM), VM configuration (SHA_VmConfig), LBFO NIC teaming and the NDIS IM platform (NET_LBFO), NDIS (NET_NDIS), the virtual switch and VFP (NET_VMswitch), the SMB client (NET_SMBcli) and the SMB server (NET_SMBsrv). At start it lists open SMB files and, on builds above 17763, enables extra SMB client and server event logs. At stop it collects the LBFO registry keys, certificate and credential information, the SMB client and server event logs and registry settings (SMB, CSC, RPC, TCP, LSA, UNC hardening), GPresult, AuditPol and SecEdit, the LanmanServer bindings check and the permissions of all shares (AccessChk); -Mode Permission adds a prompt for a share folder and file whose permissions are collected. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (capturetype=both, so virtual switch traffic is captured too; correlation=disabled), Performance Monitor counters of the SMB set (General plus SMB, every 10 seconds) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the SHA common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes and the System and Application event logs and the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives. At the end TSS builds an SDP Cluster report.

scenarios.name: SHA_HypVM
scenarios.description: Run inside the affected virtual machine for guest-side Hyper-V networking problems, for example a VM that loses network connectivity or has a failing or slow synthetic network adapter. ETW traces: Hyper-V guest networking, that is Hyper-V-Network, Netvsc and NetworkVsc, the synthetic NIC, the NDIS virtual bus and VMBus (NET_HypVM), and the NDIS layer (NET_NDIS). At start it enables the Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-NETVSC/Diagnostic event log; at stop it exports it. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the SHA common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes and the System and Application event logs and the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report. For problems on the Hyper-V host use SHA_HypHost.

scenarios.name: SHA_MScluster
scenarios.description: Run on the affected failover cluster node(s) for cluster or clustered-storage problems (membership, failover, quorum, CSV, Storage Spaces, Storage Replica, SAN paths). ETW traces: 43 Failover Clustering providers including NetFT, the cluster disk filters, Health service and Cluster-Aware Updating (SHA_MsCluster), iSCSI initiator and target (SHA_ISCSI), Multipath I/O (SHA_MPIO), the Microsoft DSM (SHA_msDSM), Storage Replica (SHA_StorageReplica), Storage Spaces (SHA_StorageSpace), the CSV file system (SHA_CSVFS), Storport (SHA_Storport), the broad storage stack (SHA_Storage) and LBFO NIC teaming (NET_LBFO). At stop it saves the cluster hive (HKLM\cluster), collects the LBFO registry keys and certificate information, and runs scripts\tss_Cluster_GetLogs.ps1, which gathers from all nodes (PowerShell remoting, admin shares) into the ClusterLogs folder: cluster and health logs (Get-ClusterLog) and System, CSVFS, Hyper-V, SMB and Storage Spaces event logs of the last 12 weeks, cluster hives, configuration and dependency reports, per-node storage, network and system data, msinfo32 and Cluster\Reports. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus its ETW providers), Performance Monitor counters of the ALL set (general, SMB, network, SQL, DC and cluster counters every 10 seconds) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the SHA common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes and the System and Application event logs and the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives. At the end TSS builds an SDP Cluster report.

scenarios.name: SPS_General
scenarios.description: Use for SharePoint Server problems when the failing area is not yet known, for example errors, slowness or hangs of SharePoint pages or services. The scenario has no ETW components and does not collect SharePoint ULS logs (use the SPS_ULS component, -SPS_ULS or -CollectLog SPS_ULS, for those); it gathers generic data with tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's internet client ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, a Windows Performance Recorder trace with the General profile (WPR General: CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilters, network and registry), Performance Monitor counters of the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk, process, SMB, network, SQL, domain controller and cluster counters every 10 seconds), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: UEX_AppLocker
scenarios.description: Use when AppLocker unexpectedly blocks or allows a program, DLL, script, Windows Installer package or packaged (Store) app, or when AppLocker rules do not seem to apply. ETW traces: AppLocker, the Application Identity (AppID) components with their logger, service trigger and reputation (AppRep) providers, the EDP AppLocker policy task and Authz access checks (UEX_AppLocker). At stop TSS saves the effective AppLocker policy (Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml, AppLockerPolicy.xml), copies the %SystemRoot%\System32\AppLocker folder (the applied rule files), records the status of the Application Identity service (AppIdSvc) and the permissions (ACL) of the Local Service account's CA certificate store key (HKEY_USERS\S-1-5-19\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\CA), and exports the four AppLocker event logs (EXE and DLL, MSI and Script, Packaged app-Deployment, Packaged app-Execution). Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode for file, registry and process activity, and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions.

scenarios.name: UEX_AppV
scenarios.description: Use for Microsoft App-V (Application Virtualization) problems, for example when a virtual application package fails to add, publish, stream, update or launch, or when the App-V client cannot reach its publishing server. ETW traces: the App-V client, client streaming UX, service log, sequencer and AppMan App-V components and the App-V management, publishing and reporting server providers (UEX_AppV). At stop TSS exports the App-V registry keys (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\AppV, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\AppV, HKCU\Software\Classes\AppV), the App-V event logs (Client Admin, Operational and Virtual Applications, Server-Management Admin, Server-Publishing Operational) plus the System and Security logs, a task list (tasklist /svc, /v, /m), AuditPol, SecEdit and GPresult output, and copies the App-V client catalog (ProgramData and AppData), the integration shortcut backups and the VFS folders (AppData and LocalAppData); per-user data comes from the account that runs TSS. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers) and Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode for file, registry and process activity. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDActivation
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to; MSRD-Collect calls it the target, while the user's own client device is the source) when Windows activation or licensing fails there. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDActivation are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -Activation. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP, AVD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_AVDActivation adds licensingdiag.exe output (its CAB is expanded), slmgr.vbs /dlv and, on a domain-joined host, the KMS servers published in DNS (_vlmcs._tcp SRV records). Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDAppAttach
