UEX_AVDAppAttach adds the App-V client Admin and Operational and the VHDMP event logs, the App Attach events filtered from the RemoteDesktopServices log, the HKLM and HKCU AppV registry keys and Get-AppvClientConfiguration, Get-AppvStatus and Get-AppxVolume output. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDAzureLocal
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host that runs on Azure Local (formerly Azure Stack HCI: AVD VMs hosted on your own hardware and connected to Azure through Azure Arc) when it fails to register, deploy or connect, or when its Arc agent misbehaves. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDAzureLocal are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role (the session host that users connect to), like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -AzureLocal. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP, AVD infrastructure incl. an Azure Local check, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days. UEX_AVDAzureLocal adds the Azure Arc agent logs (himds.log, azcmagent.log), the Guest Configuration agent, extension manager and per-extension logs, a probe of the Azure Local metadata endpoint (IMDS attested document at 169.254.169.253) with and without the system proxy and, when the Azure Connected Machine Agent is installed, azcmagent show, azcmagent check (a live outbound connectivity test to Azure) and the Hybrid agent extension applications group members. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDcli
scenarios.description: Use on the user's client device (the source: the PC that runs Windows App or the Remote Desktop client) to trace an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) connection, sign-in, disconnect or in-session problem live while you reproduce it from the user side (pair it with UEX_AVDsrv on the session host, the target). ETW traces: the Remote Desktop client (MSTSC/MSTSCAX, MSRDC and Windows App, RemoteApp and Desktop Connections, client USB redirection), authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, CAPI2, LSA), the RDP core stack and the WebRTC redirector used for Teams media optimization (UEX_AVDcli). UEX_AVDSource has no ETW providers; at stop it runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD source role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Source -Core: about 45 event logs incl. TerminalServices-RDPClient, Remote Desktop client and Windows App registry keys, logs and settings, system and network information (msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, avdnettest) and the MSRD-Diag.html health report, saved in the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDSource subfolder; if msrdc.exe is still running it first asks whether to close it (default No after 60 seconds). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon, 3096 MB ring buffer by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDCore
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to; MSRD-Collect calls it the target, while the user's own client device is the source) to collect the AVD baseline for almost any host-side problem; the other UEX_AVD* data scenarios add to it and UEX_AVDSource is its client-side counterpart. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore is data-collection-only and, at stop, runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core. It collects about 75 event logs (System, Application, Security, RDP and TerminalServices, the RemoteDesktopServices AVD agent log, AAD, GroupPolicy, SMB, WinRM, Azure guest agent), registry keys (Terminal Server, RDInfraAgent, RDAgentBootLoader, RDMonitoringAgent, policies, Lsa, Cryptography, services), AVD agent, SxS stack, Geneva monitoring, Multimedia Redirection and WebRTC install logs, Azure VM guest agent and extension logs, system information (msinfo32, DxDiag, installed software, processes and services, gpresult, Windows Update history, MDM diagnostics, dsregcmd /status), networking (ipconfig, netstat, firewall rules, proxy, avdnettest, WVDAgentUrlTool, AVD broker reachability), certificates, RDP listener permissions and local group members. It then builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP, AVD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues from the event logs of the last 5 days) with findings JSON files, the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDDiag
scenarios.description: Intended as a quick Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) health check that runs only the MSRD-Collect diagnostics report (MSRD-Diag.html), without the full data set, on a session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target). No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDDiag is data-collection-only; at stop it loads the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, queries the Azure instance metadata service (IMDS) and creates the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. Current behavior: because any -Scenario UEX_AVD* run sets MSRD-Collect's wait-for-Core-diagnostics flag and this scenario has no Core or Source component, CollectUEX_AVDDiagLog skips the diagnostics, so the scenario on its own produces no MSRD-Diag.html and essentially no data; to get the report use UEX_AVDCore on a session host or UEX_AVDSource on the user's client device (the source), which both include it. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDIME
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target) when typing with an Input Method Editor (IME, for example Japanese, Chinese or Korean input), switching keyboard layouts or input languages fails or behaves wrongly in the remote session. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDIME are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -IME. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system incl. languages, RDP, AVD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_AVDIME adds about 30 keyboard layout, IME (IMEJP, IMEKR, IMETC), text input (CTF, MTF, Input, InputMethod), speech, spelling and Control Panel\International registry keys (HKLM and HKCU), Get-Culture, Get-WinSystemLocale, Get-WinUILanguageOverride, Get-WinLanguageBarOption, Get-WinDefaultInputMethodOverride and Get-WinUserLanguageList output and folder trees of the IME and InputMethod folders. HKCU data comes from the account that runs TSS. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDMSRA
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target) when Windows Remote Assistance (msra.exe), Quick Assist or Intune Remote Help sessions with a user on that host fail. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDMSRA are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -RemoteAssist. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP incl. a Quick Assist/Remote Help check, AVD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_AVDMSRA adds the RemoteAssistance Admin and Operational and RemoteHelp/Operational event logs, the Remote Assistance and Quick Assist (HKCU) registry keys, the Offer Remote Assistance Helpers and Distributed COM Users members, the machine COM security permissions, the RemoteAssistance scheduled tasks, Remote Help installation logs and correlation vector history, the Quick Assist app package, Quick Assist and Remote Help folder trees and whoami /upn and /all. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDProfiles
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target) when user profiles, typically FSLogix profile or Office (ODFC) containers, fail to attach, users get temporary profiles or settings do not roam. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDProfiles are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -Profiles. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP incl. FSLogix checks, AVD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html connections report and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_AVDProfiles adds the User Profile Service, FSLogix Apps and CloudCache, VHDMP and filtered NTFS (events 4 and 142) event logs, FSLogix VHD compaction events, the FSLogix, Office, OneDrive, shell folder, ProfileList and Windows Search registry keys, the FSLogix logs, rules and redirections.xml, frx, Cloud Cache and pnputil output, ACLs and klist get cifs tickets for each VHDLocations share, FSLogix include/exclude groups, klist get krbtgt and whoami /upn and /all. User-specific data comes from the account that runs TSS. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDSCard
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target) when smart card redirection into the remote session or smart card sign-in fails. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDSCard are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -SmartCard. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP incl. device redirection, AVD infrastructure, identity incl. a smart card check, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_AVDSCard adds the SmartCard-Audit/Authentication, SmartCard-DeviceEnum/Operational and SmartCard-TPM-VCard-Module Admin and Operational event logs, the Kerberos/Operational log (often empty because it is disabled by default), Kerberos-KDCProxy/Operational on Windows Server and certutil -scinfo -silent output. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDSource
scenarios.description: Use on the user's client device (the source: the PC or thin client that runs Windows App or the Remote Desktop client) to collect the client-side baseline for Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) connection, sign-in or client problems; it is the counterpart of UEX_AVDCore, which runs on the session host (the target, the VM that users connect to). If msrdc.exe is running, MSRD-Collect first asks whether to close it so its logs are complete (default No after 60 seconds; Yes disconnects the user's sessions). Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDSource subfolder; user-specific data comes from the account that runs TSS. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDsrv
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target) to trace a connection, logon, session, RemoteApp, redirection, graphics or FSLogix problem live while you reproduce it (pair it with UEX_AVDcli on the user's client device, the source). UEX_AVDCore has no ETW providers; at stop it runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core: about 75 event logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, system and network information (msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, avdnettest) and the MSRD-Diag.html health and MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html connection reports, saved in the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-AVDTarget subfolder. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon, 3096 MB ring buffer by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_AVDTeams
scenarios.description: Use on an Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session host (the VM that users connect to, called the target) when Microsoft Teams in the remote session has call, meeting, media optimization (WebRTC/SlimCore redirection) or sign-in problems. No ETW tracing: UEX_AVDCore and UEX_AVDTeams are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the AVD target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine AVD -Role Target -Core -Teams. UEX_AVDCore collects the AVD Core data of the host (about 75 event logs incl. the RDP/TerminalServices and AVD agent logs, Terminal Server and AVD agent registry keys, AVD agent, SxS stack, monitoring and WebRTC redirector install logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP incl. multimedia, AVD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days, Teams), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, on an Azure VM, an Azure service status snapshot. scenarios.name: UEX_FSLogix
scenarios.description: Use on an FSLogix machine (typically an AVD or RDS session host) when profile or Office (ODFC) containers fail to attach, users get a temporary or local profile, Cloud Cache misbehaves or sign-in/sign-off is slow. ETW traces: the FSLogix service, drivers, Cloud Cache, search and tool providers plus Azure Storage (UEX_FSLogix); UEX_RDSDiag adds no ETW providers. At stop TSS exports the FSLogix Apps and CloudCache, User Profile Service, Group Policy and Terminal Services session event logs (evtx and text) and the VHDMP and SMB client/server logs (evtx), runs frx.exe version, list-redirects and list-rules, copies the *.log files from C:\ProgramData\FSLogix\Logs, exports the FSLogix (and policy), Defender exclusion, Office, OneDrive, Windows Search, ProfileList, Volatile Environment and credential provider registry keys (plus hive copies of Office, Windows Search and ProfileList), whoami /all and the members of the four FSLogix Include/Exclude local groups; UEX_RDSDiag runs the MSRD-Collect diagnostics and writes the MSRD-Diag.html health report. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_General
scenarios.description: A broad catch-all for user-experience (UEX) problems when the failing component is not yet known; it enables no component ETW trace and relies on generic tools, so switch to a specific UEX scenario once the area is clear. Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode for file, registry and process activity, a Performance Monitor (PerfMon) counter log with the ALL set (CPU, memory, disk and process counters plus SMB, network, SQL, domain controller, cluster, HTTP service, GPU and security counters) sampled every 10 seconds, Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days. At the end TSS builds an SDP NET report.

scenarios.name: UEX_Logon
scenarios.description: A lightweight, trace-only scenario for interactive sign-in and desktop start problems, for example a hang or error at the Welcome or lock screen, a credential provider (sign-in tile) problem, a temporary profile or slow first logon, or a kiosk (Assigned Access) sign-in issue. ETW traces: the sign-in stack with Winlogon, Wininit, Userinit, LogonUI and the logon controller, the credential provider framework, the Local Session Manager, the User Profile Service and profile loading, LockApp and the lock screen, Assigned Access, Token Broker and SENS (UEX_Logon); the Windows shell with Explorer, taskbar, Start, File Explorer, Cloud Experience Host and Settings components (PRF_Shell); and the Local Security Authority (lsass) with its LSA, LSAIso, Netlogon, Vault, gMSA and KDS providers (ADS_LSA). It runs no Procmon, no PSR and no network capture. Because CollectComponentLog is not set, the registry and file data of the Logon and Shell components is not collected (add -CollectComponentLog if you need it); at stop TSS adds only the default basic log.

scenarios.name: UEX_MDAG
scenarios.description: Use for Microsoft Defender Application Guard (MDAG) problems, for example when the isolated Edge or Office container fails to start, crashes or has no network access. ETW traces: Application Guard on the host (UEX_MDAG), in two files: MDAGHost with the HVSI service, manager, settings, policy evaluator and filters, the RDP client components that display the container and the Hyper-V compute, VMBus, worker and container libraries; HostFirewall with the Windows Firewall service, Base Filtering Engine and WFP providers. At start TSS saves hcsdiag list, sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\HVSI DisableResetContainer=1, resumes the MDAG container if needed (wdagtool.exe resume), shares the log folder into it and starts an ETW trace (config\ContainerProviders.wprp profile) and a netsh InternetClient_dbg capture inside the container. At stop it copies both container traces (ContainerTrace.etl, ContainerNetTrace.etl) to the host, collects the container's ipconfig /all, task lists, System, Application, AppXDeploymentServer and CodeIntegrity event logs and a licensingdiag cab, sets DisableResetContainer to 0 and saves hcsdiag list again; the container steps are skipped when no MDAG container exists. Tools: a netsh trace with the virtualization, wireless_dbg and InternetClient_dbg scenarios plus 16 extra providers added by GUID (WinNAT and NAT, Host Network Service and its plugins, VmSwitch, Hyper-V synthetic NIC, NetSetup, container setup, firewall policy), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode, Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video.

scenarios.name: UEX_MMC
scenarios.description: Use when Microsoft Management Console (mmc.exe) or one of its snap-ins fails to load, shows an error or crashes, especially .NET (MMC 3.0) snap-ins with assembly load or version errors. ETW traces: MMC (UEX_MMC); UEX_Fusion adds no ETW providers but turns on .NET Framework assembly binding (Fusion) logging. At start TSS sets ForceLog, LogFailures, LogResourceBinds, EnableLog and LogPath under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Fusion so that binding logs are written to the FusionLogs subfolder of the TSS log folder, and asks you to close and reopen the affected program so that it picks up the setting. At stop it removes these Fusion registry values again and saves the registered snap-ins (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\MMC\SnapIns), the installed .NET Framework versions (NET Framework Setup\NDP registry) and a recursive file listing of C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET. Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode for file, registry and process activity, and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the user's actions.

scenarios.name: UEX_MSRA
scenarios.description: Use when a Windows Remote Assistance (msra.exe) or desktop shadowing session fails to start, connect or take control of the remote screen. ETW traces: Remote Assistance with its RDP and PNRP providers (UEX_MSRA), RDS shadowing (RdpSA) and the Desktop Sharing sharer and viewer (UEX_Shadowing), COM/DCOM, RPC and WinRT activation (UEX_COM; with -EnableCOMDebug TSS also sets HKLM\Software\Microsoft\OLE\Tracing ExecutablesToTrace=* at start and removes it at stop) and the authentication bundle with Kerberos, NTLM/CredSSP, LSA, Schannel, NGC (Windows Hello), smart card, biometrics, credential providers, DPAPI and web authentication (ADS_Auth). At start ADS_Auth also enables about 25 authentication event logs (CAPI2, Kerberos, WebAuthN, AAD, User Device Registration, Hello for Business, DPAPI and others, exporting or clearing some first), turns on LSA, NegoExtender, Pku2u, LSP, Kerberos (clients), Netlogon, Group Policy service and certificate enrollment debug logging, saves dsregcmd /status, klist (user and SYSTEM), tasklist, services, netstat and DNS cache snapshots in PreTraceLogs and flushes the DNS cache. Because CollectComponentLog is not set, the ADS_Auth stop step that exports these logs and switches the debug settings off does not run: the settings stay enabled after TSS stops and the extra logs are not collected (add -CollectComponentLog to avoid this); the COM data collection is skipped as well. Tools: a netsh packet capture, Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots.

scenarios.name: UEX_PowerShell
scenarios.description: Use for Windows PowerShell or PowerShell remoting problems: a script, module or cmdlet fails or behaves unexpectedly, or a remote session (Enter-PSSession, Invoke-Command) over WinRM cannot connect or authenticate. ETW traces: Windows PowerShell and PowerShell Web Access (UEX_PowerShell) and Windows Remote Management with the WinRM, WinHTTP and HTTP service providers (UEX_WinRMBase; -WinRMProvList adds optional provider groups such as Kerberos, NTLM, CredSSP, Schannel or HTTPSYS), which also saves a task list at start and stop. At stop TSS exports the PowerShell Admin, Operational and PowerShellCore/Operational event logs and a PowerShell snapshot taken from the session that runs TSS: installed and loaded modules, repositories, $PSVersionTable, variables, the profile script, PS drives, PowerShell host processes, providers, execution context, powershell.config.json, the execution policy list and all available commands. It also runs scripts\WinRM-Collect.ps1 -Logs (stopped after 30 minutes) into a WinRM-Results folder: WinRM configuration and listeners, process dumps of the WinRM service host and wsmprovhost.exe, event forwarding subscriptions, WinRM, security and HTTP registry keys, firewall rules, netsh http settings, certificates, GPResult, about 17 event logs and a WinRM-Diag.txt health check. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon) in ring-buffer mode and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots.

scenarios.name: UEX_Print
scenarios.description: Use for printing problems on a print client or print server when no network capture is needed: print jobs that fail or stay in the queue, wrong or garbled output, printer or driver installation failures, Universal Print problems or spooler crashes. ETW traces: the whole printing stack with about 190 providers (UEX_Print), covering the spooler service and client (spoolsv, localspl, win32spl, winspool), print drivers and render filters, port monitors (TCP/IP, USB, WSD, LPR, IPP), XPS and Print to PDF, print dialogs, Universal Print, Terminal Services printer redirection, scanning (eSCL, WIA) and printer discovery. At start TSS enables the PrintService Admin, Operational and Debug event logs (original settings restored at stop) and saves build information, Get-PrinterDriver output and a task list. At stop it collects into a PrintLog folder: 12 event logs (System, Application, PrintService, PrintBRM, DeviceSetupManager, TerminalServices-Printers and the Universal Print connector logs), spooler file versions, printer registry exports (HKCU Printers and Devices, HKLM Print, printer policies, Client Side Rendering, Control\Print, USBPRINT, DriverDatabase, KIR feature overrides, per-user Universal Print PrinterProvisioning), sc queryex spooler, netstat -anob, ipconfig /all, driverquery /v, the prnmngr, prndrvr, prnjobs and prnport.vbs listings, tree listings of Inf, DriverStore and spool, pnputil output, oem*.inf files, setupapi logs and wiatrace.log, plus process dumps of spoolsv, splwow64 and PrintIsolationHost (if running), the printer Ports and Printers registry keys, and gpresult, auditpol and secedit output. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog). It runs no network capture, no Procmon and no PSR; use UEX_PrintFull when you need them.

scenarios.name: UEX_PrintFull
scenarios.description: Use for printing problems that also need network and process context, for example printing through a print server or to a network printer, driver download failures, Remote Desktop redirected printing or spooler problems caused by third party components. ETW traces: the whole printing stack with about 190 providers (UEX_Print), covering the spooler service and client, print drivers and render filters, port monitors (TCP/IP, USB, WSD, LPR, IPP), XPS and Print to PDF, print dialogs, Universal Print, Terminal Services printer redirection, scanning and printer discovery. At start TSS enables the PrintService Admin, Operational and Debug event logs (restored at stop) and saves build information, Get-PrinterDriver output and a task list. At stop it collects into a PrintLog folder: 12 event logs (System, Application, PrintService, PrintBRM, DeviceSetupManager, TerminalServices-Printers and the Universal Print connector logs), spooler file versions, printer and driver registry exports (HKCU and HKLM print keys, printer policies, Client Side Rendering, USBPRINT, DriverDatabase, KIR feature overrides, per-user Universal Print settings), spooler service, netstat, ipconfig and driverquery output, the prn*.vbs printer, driver, job and port listings, tree listings of Inf, DriverStore and spool, pnputil output, oem*.inf files, setupapi logs and wiatrace.log, process dumps of spoolsv, splwow64 and PrintIsolationHost (if running), the printer Ports and Printers registry keys, and gpresult, auditpol and secedit output. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon, ring buffer 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_QuickAssist
scenarios.description: Use when a Quick Assist session fails to start, connect, or show or control the remote screen; it also covers Windows Remote Assistance (msra.exe) and Remote Help data. ETW traces: Quick Assist with the Remote Desktop ActiveX client and RDP core providers (UEX_QuickAssist), Windows Remote Assistance with PNRP (Easy Connect) and its RDP screen sharing components (UEX_MSRA), and the WebView provider used for the embedded web content (UEX_Webview). UEX_RDSMSRA adds no ETW providers; at stop it runs the MSRD-Collect RemoteAssist data collection: the Remote Assistance and Remote Help event logs, the Remote Assistance and Quick Assist registry keys, membership of the Offer Remote Assistance Helpers and Distributed COM Users groups, the machine-wide COM (DCOM) access and launch permissions, the RemoteAssistance scheduled tasks, Remote Help installation logs, the Quick Assist AppX package, whoami /upn and /all, and file trees of the Quick Assist and Remote Help install folders. It also creates the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report and saves the nested Active Directory group membership of each logged-on user (NestedGroups.txt). Tools: a netsh trace with the InternetClient_dbg scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon, ring buffer 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSActivation
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS server or session host when Windows itself does not activate (KMS or MAK activation errors, "Windows is not activated"); RDS CAL licensing data comes from the Core part. No ETW tracing: two data-collection-only components run the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the RDS host (Target) role and save the results in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder. UEX_RDSActivation collects Windows activation data: licensingdiag.exe /cab (unpacked), cscript slmgr.vbs /dlv and, on domain members, the KMS servers published in DNS (_vlmcs._tcp SRV records). UEX_RDSCore adds the baseline RDS host data set: about 95 event logs (on servers incl. TerminalServices-Licensing), RDS/RDP and TermServLicensing registry keys, TerminalServices WMI settings, networking and system information and data for installed RDS roles (on a license server also the RD Licensing database report). Then the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report (with activation and RDS licensing checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections are built. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDScli
scenarios.description: Use on the user's client computer (the Source, i.e. the machine the user connects from, where mstsc or the Remote Desktop app runs) to capture a failing or slow RDS connection or a RemoteApp and Desktop Connections (RD Web feed) problem while you reproduce it. ETW traces: the Remote Desktop client stack (UEX_RDScli): mstsc/mstscax client core and shell, RD Gateway client, RemoteFX codec, USB redirection and feed subscription providers plus the client event channels, RDP core, the RemoteApp and Desktop Connections workspace, and authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, LSA, CAPI2). At stop the data-collection-only component UEX_RDSSource runs the client-side (Source) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 45 event logs incl. TerminalServices-RDPClient, Remote Desktop client registry keys, networking and system information) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report for the client. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSCore
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS server (RD Session Host, Connection Broker, Gateway, Licensing or Web Access server, i.e. the host side that users connect to, called Target) as the first collection for almost any RDS case, without a live repro trace; most other UEX_RDS* scenarios include it. No ETW tracing: the data-collection-only component UEX_RDSCore runs the Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the host (Target) role and saves it in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder: about 95 event logs (System, Application, Security, TerminalServices LocalSessionManager, RemoteConnectionManager and Printers, RdpCoreTS, CAPI2, NTLM, SMB, GroupPolicy, AAD and more), RDS/RDP registry keys (Terminal Server, TermServLicensing, Winlogon, Lsa, policies, services), TerminalServices WMI settings, RDP listener permissions, qwinsta and chgport output, members of Administrators, Remote Desktop Users and the RDS server groups, networking (ipconfig, netstat, routes, firewall rules, proxy, nltest), system information (gpresult, installed roles and features, services, drivers, certificate stores, setspn TERMSRV/WSMAN, dsregcmd /status, Windows Update history, setup and CBS logs) and, on servers, data for each installed RDS role: Connection Broker deployment data (GetFarmData.txt from the RemoteDesktop module) and RDMS/WID logs, Gateway policies and NPS events, the RD Licensing database report and RD Web Access configuration and logs. It then builds the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report (system, RDP, identity, networking, security and known-issue checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSDiag
scenarios.description: Intended as a quick RDS health check: the data-collection-only component UEX_RDSDiag should build only the MSRD-Collect diagnostics report (MSRD-Diag.html with system, RDP, identity, networking, security and known-issue checks) for the RDS host (Target), without collecting other data. Known issue in the current code: every -Scenario UEX_RDS* run now leaves the report to a Core or Source component and this scenario has none, so UEX_RDSDiag skips the report and the run produces no MSRD-Collect data. Until this is fixed, use UEX_RDSCore on the host or UEX_RDSSource on the client (or add -UEX_RDSSource to this scenario on a client), which build the same report together with their Core data. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSIME
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS host when typing with an Input Method Editor (Japanese, Chinese or Korean IME), keyboard layouts or input languages misbehave in a Remote Desktop session. No ETW tracing: two data-collection-only components run the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the RDS host (Target) role and save the results in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder. UEX_RDSIME collects IME, input and language registry keys (Control Panel\International, Keyboard Layout(s), CTF, IME, IMEJP/IMEKR/IMETC, Input, InputMethod, MTF, Speech, Spelling), folder trees of the user and system IME folders, and the culture, system locale, UI language override, language bar, default input method and user language list (Get-Culture, Get-WinSystemLocale, Get-WinUserLanguageList and related cmdlets); per-user data comes from the account that runs TSS. UEX_RDSCore adds the baseline RDS host data set (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys and TerminalServices WMI settings, networking and system information, and data for installed RDS roles). Then the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections are built. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSMSRA
scenarios.description: Use when Windows Remote Assistance (msra.exe), Quick Assist or Intune Remote Help sessions fail to start, connect or be offered. No ETW tracing: two data-collection-only components run the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) and save the results in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder. UEX_RDSMSRA collects the RemoteAssistance Admin/Operational and RemoteHelp/Operational event logs, the Remote Assistance (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance) and QuickAssist registry keys, members of Offer Remote Assistance Helpers and Distributed COM Users, the DCOM default and machine access/launch permissions (COMSecurity.txt), the RemoteAssistance scheduled tasks, Remote Help installation logs and correlation vector history, the Quick Assist AppX package, whoami /upn and /all and the Quick Assist and Remote Help program folder trees; TSS adds the nested Active Directory group tree of every user with running processes (NestedGroups.txt, needs the ActiveDirectory PowerShell module). By default this uses the host (Target) role; only if -UEX_RDSSource is also given it uses the client (Source) role and skips the MSRA event logs, registry, groups, permissions and tasks. UEX_RDSCore adds the baseline RDS host data set (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys and TerminalServices WMI settings, networking and system information, and data for installed RDS roles). Then the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report (with Quick Assist checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections are built. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSProfiles
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS host when user profiles do not load, users get a temporary profile, sign-in is slow because of the profile, or FSLogix profile or Office containers fail to attach or save. No ETW tracing: two data-collection-only components run the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the RDS host (Target) role and save the results in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder. UEX_RDSProfiles collects the User Profile Service, FSLogix Apps and CloudCache, VHDMP and NTFS event logs, the ProfileList, Shell Folders, OneDrive, Office, Windows Search, Volatile Environment and FSLogix registry keys, whoami /upn and /all, klist get krbtgt, the list of profile folders and FSLogix details: frx version, list-redirects and list-rules, the redirections XML, FSLogix logs and rules files, Cloud Cache disk and provider information, members of the FSLogix include/exclude groups, a PnP state export, profile location checks and a virtual disk registry consistency check. UEX_RDSCore adds the baseline RDS host data set (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys and TerminalServices WMI settings, networking and system information, and data for installed RDS roles). Then the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report (with FSLogix checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections are built. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSSCard
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS host when smart card sign-in to a Remote Desktop session or smart card redirection into the session fails. No ETW tracing: two data-collection-only components run the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) and save the results in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder. UEX_RDSSCard collects the SmartCard-Audit/Authentication, SmartCard-DeviceEnum/Operational and SmartCard-TPM-VCard-Module event logs, the Kerberos/Operational log (and Kerberos-KDCProxy/Operational on servers) and certutil -scinfo -silent (readers, cards and their certificates). By default this uses the host (Target) role; only if -UEX_RDSSource is also given it uses the client (Source) role and skips the Kerberos logs. UEX_RDSCore adds the baseline RDS host data set (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys and TerminalServices WMI settings, networking and system information, and data for installed RDS roles). Then the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report (with smart card checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections are built. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSSource
scenarios.description: Use on the client computer the user connects from (the Source, where mstsc or the Remote Desktop app runs) to collect its Remote Desktop configuration, logs and a health report without a live repro trace; it is the client-side counterpart of UEX_RDSCore, which runs on the RDS host (Target). No ETW tracing: the data-collection-only component UEX_RDSSource runs the Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the client (Source) role and saves it in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder: about 45 event logs (System, Application, Security, TerminalServices-RDPClient/Operational, RemoteApp and Desktop Connections, ClientUSBDevices, CAPI2, NTLM, SMBClient, AAD and more), Remote Desktop client registry keys (Terminal Server Client, MSLicensing, RdClientRadc, Remote Desktop) plus policies, Lsa, Internet Settings and services keys, networking (ipconfig, netstat, routes, firewall rules, proxy, nltest, LAN/WLAN settings and WLAN report) and system information (gpresult, services, drivers, installed features, dsregcmd /status, Windows Update history, setup and CBS logs, MDM info). It then builds the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report for the client, including Remote Desktop client checks. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSsrv
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS server, usually the RD Session Host, to capture a server-side RDS problem while you reproduce it when you do not know which RDS role is involved; it traces all RDS roles on that machine. ETW traces: the broad RDS server stack (UEX_RDSsrv): RDP core, RD Session Host and user logon, authentication, RemoteApp and app publishing, clipboard, device, audio and printer redirection, RemoteFX graphics, Connection Broker, Gateway, Licensing, RD Management Service (RDMS), Virtual IP, Hyper-V, VM host agent, MultiPoint and WMI/WinRM providers; with -Mode Basic a lighter set without the audio, MultiPoint, printing and WMI/WinRM providers is used. At start the UEX_RDSsrv component turns on RDMS UI logging (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\RDMS) and the CAPI2/Operational event log; at stop it copies RDMSDeploymentUI.txt and RdmsUI-trace.log, deletes that RDMS key and restores the CAPI2 log settings. UEX_RDSCore then runs the host-side (Target) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry, networking, system and installed RDS role data) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html and MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html reports. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSrdgw
scenarios.description: Use on the RD Gateway server (the role that tunnels RDP over HTTPS so users can connect from the internet) when connections through the gateway fail or drop (authorization policies, certificates, authentication, transport) while you reproduce it. ETW traces (UEX_RDSrdgw): the RD Gateway service (AaEdgeService, AaTsPP, RemoteDesktop.Gateway) with the TerminalServices-Gateway event channel, WMI/WinRM and authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, LSA, CAPI2). At stop UEX_RDSCore runs the host-side (Target) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 95 event logs incl. TerminalServices-Gateway, RDS/RDP registry keys incl. TerminalServerGateway, networking and system information); on a gateway it also saves the connection and resource authorization policies (CAP/RAP), RADIUS, load-balancing and server settings from WMI and the NPS events filtered from the Security log, and builds the MSRD-Diag.html report (with Gateway checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSrdcb
scenarios.description: Use on the RD Connection Broker (the role that places users on a session host, load-balances and reconnects them and stores the RDS deployment configuration) for session placement, load-balancing, reconnect or deployment management problems while you reproduce them. ETW traces (UEX_RDSrdcb): the Connection Broker (SessionBroker, VM plugin, central database plugin, RdvVmCore) with the SessionBroker and RemoteApp and Desktop Connection Management event channels, RD Session Host session components, the RD Management Service (RDMS), WMI/WinRM and authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, LSA, CAPI2). At stop UEX_RDSCore runs the host-side (Target) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys, networking and system information); on a Connection Broker it also saves the deployment data from the RemoteDesktop module (GetFarmData.txt: servers, collections, RemoteApps, certificates, licensing, high availability), Workspace and Session Directory WMI data, RDMSDeploymentUI.txt, tssesdir XML files and WID error logs, and builds the MSRD-Diag.html report (with Connection Broker checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSrdwa
scenarios.description: Use on the RD Web Access server (the IIS site /RDWeb and the feed that publish RemoteApps and desktops to browsers and to RemoteApp and Desktop Connections) when the web page, its sign-in or the feed subscription fails while you reproduce it. ETW traces (UEX_RDSrdwa): RemoteApp and desktop publishing (TSCPUBSvr, tspubfilter, TSPublishing WMI provider and icon helper), WMI/WinRM and authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, LSA, CAPI2). At stop UEX_RDSCore runs the host-side (Target) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys, networking and system information); on a Web Access server it also saves the IIS configuration (appcmd list config), the RD Web Access logs (%windir%\web\rdweb\App_Data\rdweb*.log) and the members of the Windows Authorization Access Group, and builds the MSRD-Diag.html report (with Web Access checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSrdls
scenarios.description: Use on the RD Licensing server (the role that issues RDS client access licenses, CALs, to session hosts) for CAL issuance, license server activation, license database or license-server-not-found problems while you reproduce them. ETW traces (UEX_RDSrdls): the license server service (lserver, RDS licensing telemetry, TLS brand and WMI trace) with the TerminalServices-Licensing event channel, WMI/WinRM and authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, LSA, CAPI2). At stop UEX_RDSCore runs the host-side (Target) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 95 event logs incl. TerminalServices-Licensing, RDS/RDP registry keys incl. TermServLicensing, networking and system information); on a license server it also saves an HTML report of the license database (installed key packs and issued licenses, rdls_LicenseInfo.html) and, on domain members, the members of the Terminal Server License Servers group, and builds the MSRD-Diag.html report (with licensing checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSrdsh
scenarios.description: Use on an RD Session Host (the server that hosts the users' desktop and RemoteApp sessions) for session creation, sign-in, black screen, disconnect, redirection, printing or graphics problems inside sessions while you reproduce them. ETW traces (UEX_RDSrdsh): RDP core, RD Session Host (Local Session Manager, TermService, broker client, licensing policy) with their event channels, user logon (Winlogon, User Profile Service, Group Policy, logon UI), authentication, RemoteApp (RAIL), clipboard, device and USB redirection, audio and media redirection, print spooler and RD printing, RemoteFX graphics, Virtual IP, Hyper-V and VM host agent channels and WMI/WinRM. At stop UEX_RDSCore runs the host-side (Target) Core data set of the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys, networking and system information); on a session host it also saves the licensing grace period, discovered license servers, Virtual IP settings, RCM key permissions and the licensing scheduled tasks, and builds the MSRD-Diag.html report (with Session Host, RDP listener and redirection checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (ring buffer, 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_RDSTeams
scenarios.description: Use on an RDS host when Microsoft Teams misbehaves inside a Remote Desktop session (sign-in, crashes, calls, audio or camera problems, media optimization). No ETW tracing: two data-collection-only components run the bundled MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) and save the results in an MSRD-Collect-<computer> subfolder. UEX_RDSTeams collects the Teams registry keys (HKCU and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Teams and the RDWebRTCSvc service key), the Teams AppX package information and the new Teams logs from the user profile (MSTeams Support Logs and PROD-WebLogs in Downloads, skylib logs); per-user data comes from the account that runs TSS. By default this uses the host (Target) role; only if -UEX_RDSSource is also given it uses the client (Source) role, skips the registry keys and collects the client-side TeamsVDI logs instead. UEX_RDSCore adds the baseline RDS host data set (about 95 event logs, RDS/RDP registry keys and TerminalServices WMI settings, networking and system information, and data for installed RDS roles). Then the MSRD-Diag.html diagnostics report (with Teams checks) and the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of incoming connections are built. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_ServerManager
scenarios.description: Use when Server Manager cannot add, refresh or manage local or remote servers (for example manageability or data retrieval errors) or fails to deploy roles and features. Server Manager relies on WinRM and WMI, so both are traced as well. ETW traces: the Server Manager management, multi-machine, deployment and remoting configuration providers (UEX_ServerManager), WinRM with WinHTTP and HTTP.sys (UEX_WinRMBase) and WMI activity (UEX_WMIBase; before build 26063 it also includes the WMI core and WMI_Tracing providers). TSS saves a task list at start and stop; on build 26063 or later it also runs a WMI arbitrator task dump (winmgmt /dumptasks arb) in a background job during the trace. At stop it runs scripts\WinRM-Collect.ps1 -Logs (WinRM configuration, listeners and plugins, WinRM-Diag.txt checks, dumps of the WinRM service, wsmprovhost and Windows Admin Center processes, 17 event logs including WinRM, CAPI2, PowerShell and the Server Manager logs, WinRM, HTTP, Schannel and LSA registry keys, SPNs, certificates, netsh http settings, firewall rules, the Server Manager ServerList.xml and gpresult) and scripts\Wmi-Collect.ps1 -Logs (dumps of the WMI service, WmiPrvSE and other provider hosts, WMI, OLE and RPC registry keys, the Application, System and WMI-Activity logs, provider host, quota and event subscription details, service configuration and the WMI-RPC-DCOM-Diag.txt checks); each script may run up to 30 minutes. Tools: a netsh packet capture and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots.

scenarios.name: UEX_TSched
scenarios.description: Use when scheduled tasks do not start, fail with an error code, run under the wrong account or do not trigger as expected (time, logon, idle or event triggers); the shell and sign-in traces help with logon-triggered or interactive tasks. ETW traces: the Task Scheduler service and engine with the time broker, system events broker, broker infrastructure and UBPM trigger providers (UEX_TSched), the Windows shell with about 130 providers (PRF_Shell) and the sign-in stack with about 65 providers for Winlogon, LogonUI, credential providers, user profiles, lock screen and Assigned Access (UEX_Logon). TSS saves a task list at start and stop. At stop it runs scripts\Sched-Collect.ps1 -Logs (up to 30 minutes): dumps of the svchost processes hosting the Schedule and SystemEventsBroker services, Tasks.csv with every task's state, last run time, decoded last result and next run time, copies of the task definitions (Windows\Tasks and System32\Tasks), the Schedule registry key, the Application, System and TaskScheduler Operational and Maintenance event logs, the Schedule service configuration, whoami /all, cmdkey /list, hotfixes and gpresult. It also collects shell data (Explorer policies and file associations, the Explorer registry hives, the app resolver cache and the Start menu shortcuts, PRF_Shell) and sign-in data (Winlogon, authentication and Assigned Access registry keys, Get-AssignedAccess, Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers and Get-StartApps, UEX_Logon). Tools: a WPR trace with the General profile (CPU, disk and file I/O, handles, minifilters, network and registry), Process Monitor (Procmon, ring buffer 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots.

scenarios.name: UEX_W365Activation
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user; MSRD-Collect calls it the target, while the user's own client device is the source) when Windows activation or licensing fails on it. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core and UEX_W365Activation are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core -Activation. UEX_W365Core collects the W365 Core data of the Cloud PC (about 75 event logs incl. RDP/TerminalServices, the RemoteDesktopServices agent log and CodeIntegrity, Terminal Server and RD agent registry keys, RD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, Azure guest agent logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system incl. activation/licensing, RDP, RD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, if the Azure region can be detected, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_W365Activation adds licensingdiag.exe output (its CAB is expanded), slmgr.vbs /dlv and, if the Cloud PC is domain-joined, the KMS servers published in DNS (_vlmcs._tcp SRV records). Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365cli
scenarios.description: Use on the user's client device (the source: the PC that runs Windows App or the Remote Desktop client) to trace a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC connection, sign-in, disconnect or in-session problem live while you reproduce it from the user side (pair it with UEX_W365srv on the Cloud PC, the target). ETW traces: the Remote Desktop client (MSTSC/MSTSCAX, MSRDC and Windows App, RemoteApp and Desktop Connections, client USB redirection), authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, CAPI2, LSA), the RDP core stack and the WebRTC redirector used for Teams media optimization (UEX_W365cli). UEX_W365Source has no ETW providers; at stop it runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 source role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Source -Core: about 45 event logs incl. TerminalServices-RDPClient, Remote Desktop client, Windows App and Windows 365 registry keys, logs and settings, system and network information (msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, avdnettest) and the MSRD-Diag.html health report, saved in the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Source subfolder; if msrdc.exe is still running it first asks whether to close it (default No after 60 seconds). Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon, 3096 MB ring buffer by default), Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots and a screen video. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_W365Core
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user; MSRD-Collect calls it the target, while the user's own client device is the source) to collect the W365 baseline for almost any Cloud PC-side problem; the other UEX_W365* data scenarios add to it and UEX_W365Source is its client-side counterpart. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core is data-collection-only and, at stop, runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core. It collects about 75 event logs (System, Application, Security, RDP and TerminalServices, the RemoteDesktopServices agent log, CodeIntegrity, AAD, GroupPolicy, SMB, WinRM), registry keys (Terminal Server, RDInfraAgent, RDAgentBootLoader, RDMonitoringAgent, HybridCompute, policies, Lsa, Cryptography, services), RD agent, SxS stack, Geneva monitoring, Multimedia Redirection and WebRTC install logs, Azure guest agent logs, the AI-enabled Cloud PC package list, system information (msinfo32, DxDiag, installed software, gpresult, Windows Update history, MDM diagnostics, dsregcmd /status), networking (ipconfig, netstat, firewall rules, proxy, avdnettest, WVDAgentUrlTool, broker reachability), certificates and RDP listener permissions. It then builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP, RD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues from the event logs of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, if the Azure region can be detected, an Azure service status snapshot. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365Diag
scenarios.description: Intended as a quick Windows 365 (W365) health check that runs only the MSRD-Collect diagnostics report (MSRD-Diag.html), without the full data set, on a Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target). No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Diag is data-collection-only; at stop it loads the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, queries the Azure instance metadata service (IMDS) and creates the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. Current behavior: because any -Scenario UEX_W365* run sets MSRD-Collect's wait-for-Core-diagnostics flag and this scenario has no Core or Source component, CollectUEX_W365DiagLog skips the diagnostics, so the scenario on its own produces no MSRD-Diag.html and essentially no data; to get the report use UEX_W365Core on the Cloud PC or UEX_W365Source on the user's client device (the source), which both include it. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365IME
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target) when typing with an Input Method Editor (IME, for example Japanese, Chinese or Korean input), switching keyboard layouts or input languages fails or behaves wrongly in the remote session. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core and UEX_W365IME are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core -IME. UEX_W365Core collects the W365 Core data of the Cloud PC (about 75 event logs incl. RDP/TerminalServices, the RemoteDesktopServices agent log and CodeIntegrity, Terminal Server and RD agent registry keys, RD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system incl. languages, RDP, RD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, if the Azure region can be detected, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_W365IME adds about 30 keyboard layout, IME, text input (CTF, MTF, Input, InputMethod), speech, spelling and Control Panel\International registry keys (HKLM and HKCU), Get-Culture, Get-WinSystemLocale, Get-WinUILanguageOverride, Get-WinLanguageBarOption, Get-WinDefaultInputMethodOverride and Get-WinUserLanguageList output and folder trees of the IME and InputMethod folders. HKCU data comes from the account that runs TSS. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365MSRA
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target) when Windows Remote Assistance (msra.exe), Quick Assist or Intune Remote Help sessions with the user of that Cloud PC fail. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core and UEX_W365MSRA are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core -RemoteAssist. UEX_W365MSRA adds the RemoteAssistance Admin and Operational and RemoteHelp/Operational event logs, the Remote Assistance and Quick Assist (HKCU) registry keys, the Offer Remote Assistance Helpers and Distributed COM Users members, the machine COM security permissions, the RemoteAssistance scheduled tasks, Remote Help installation logs and correlation vector history, the Quick Assist app package, Quick Assist and Remote Help folder trees and whoami /upn and /all. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365Profiles
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target) when the user profile does not load, a temporary profile is used, or known folders, OneDrive, Office or Windows Search settings misbehave. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core and UEX_W365Profiles are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core -Profiles. UEX_W365Core collects the W365 Core data of the Cloud PC (about 75 event logs incl. UEX_W365Profiles adds the User Profile Service/Operational event log, the Office, OneDrive, Shell Folders, User Shell Folders, ProfileList, Windows Search and Volatile Environment registry keys, the list of profile folders, klist get krbtgt and whoami /upn and /all. Most FSLogix items of the MSRD-Collect Profiles data (FSLogix logs, event logs, registry, VHD locations) are collected only for AVD and RDS, not for W365. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365SCard
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target) when smart card redirection into the Cloud PC session or smart card sign-in fails. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core and UEX_W365SCard are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core -SmartCard. UEX_W365Core collects the W365 Core data of the Cloud PC (about 75 event logs incl. RDP/TerminalServices, the RemoteDesktopServices agent log and CodeIntegrity, Terminal Server and RD agent registry keys, RD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP incl. device redirection, RD infrastructure, identity incl. a smart card check, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, if the Azure region can be detected, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_W365SCard adds the SmartCard-Audit/Authentication, SmartCard-DeviceEnum/Operational and SmartCard-TPM-VCard-Module Admin and Operational event logs, the Kerberos/Operational log (often empty because it is disabled by default) and certutil -scinfo -silent output. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_W365Source
scenarios.description: Use on the user's client device (the source: the PC or thin client that runs Windows App or the Remote Desktop client) to collect the client-side baseline for Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC connection, sign-in or client problems; it is the counterpart of UEX_W365Core, which runs on the Cloud PC (the target, the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for the user). No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Source is data-collection-only and, at stop, runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 source role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Source -Core. It collects about 45 event logs (System, Application, Security, TerminalServices-RDPClient, RemoteApp and Desktop Connections, client USB devices, ClipESU on Windows 10), registry keys (Terminal Server Client, MSRDC, RdClientRadc, Windows365, WindowsApp, policies, services), Remote Desktop client and Windows App logs and settings (rdclientwpf, DiagOutputDir, Windows App settings, the CloudPC folder), Windows Cloud Input Protection logs and TPM information, system information (msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, Windows Update history, dsregcmd /status) and networking (ipconfig, netstat, firewall rules, proxy, WLAN settings and report, avdnettest, rdweb.wvd.microsoft.com reachability). It then builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, Remote Desktop clients, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days). If msrdc.exe is running, MSRD-Collect first asks whether to close it to flush its logs (default No after 60 seconds; Yes disconnects the user's sessions). Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Source subfolder; user-specific data comes from the account that runs TSS. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target) to trace a connection, logon, session, RemoteApp, redirection or graphics problem live while you reproduce it (pair it with UEX_W365cli on the user's client device, the source). ETW traces: the RDP core stack, session host services (Local Session Manager, Remote Connection Manager), user logon (Winlogon, User Profile Service, Group Policy), authentication (CredSSP, Kerberos, NTLM, Schannel, CAPI2), RemoteApp (RAIL), clipboard, device and USB redirection, audio, print spooler, graphics, the Teams WebRTC redirector and WMI/WinRM (UEX_W365srv). UEX_W365Core has no ETW providers; at stop it runs the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core: about 75 event logs, Terminal Server and RD agent registry keys, RD agent, SxS stack and monitoring logs, system and network information (msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, avdnettest) and the MSRD-Diag.html health and MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html connection reports, saved in the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. Tools: a netsh trace with the NetConnection scenario (packet capture plus the scenario's ETW providers), Process Monitor (Procmon, 3096 MB ring buffer by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots. Runs the NET common tasks instead of the default basic log: system, network, SMB, service, Kerberos ticket and domain (nltest) snapshots at start and stop; at start it clears the DNS, Kerberos and DFS referral caches and re-registers NetBIOS names (use -noClearCache to skip this); at stop it adds hotfixes, the System and Application event logs, the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM registry hives and a memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) younger than 2 days.

scenarios.name: UEX_W365Teams
scenarios.description: Use on a Windows 365 (W365) Cloud PC (the personal Windows VM that Microsoft hosts for a user, called the target) when Microsoft Teams in the Cloud PC session has call, meeting, media optimization (WebRTC/SlimCore redirection) or sign-in problems. No ETW tracing: UEX_W365Core and UEX_W365Teams are data-collection-only and, at stop, run the embedded MSRD-Collect tool (scripts\MSRD-Collect) for the W365 target role, like MSRD-Collect -Machine W365 -Role Target -Core -Teams. UEX_W365Core collects the W365 Core data of the Cloud PC (about 75 event logs incl. RDP/TerminalServices, the RemoteDesktopServices agent log and CodeIntegrity, Terminal Server and RD agent registry keys, RD agent, SxS stack, monitoring and WebRTC redirector install logs, msinfo32, DxDiag, gpresult, networking incl. avdnettest and broker reachability, certificates) and builds the MSRD-Diag.html health report (system, RDP incl. multimedia, RD infrastructure, identity, networking, security, known issues of the last 5 days, Teams), the MSRD-Diag-RDConnections.html report of RDP connections in the last 14 days and, if the Azure region can be detected, an Azure service status snapshot. UEX_W365Teams adds the host-side Teams logs of the account that runs TSS (MSTeams Support Logs and PROD-WebLogs from Downloads, new Teams skylib logs), the HKLM and HKCU Teams registry keys, the RDWebRTCSvc service key and the Teams app package list (Get-AppxPackage *Teams*); client-side Teams VDI logs are not collected by this scenario. Output goes to the MSRD-Collect-<computer>-W365Target subfolder. TSS does not wait for a repro (noRepro): it starts, collects and stops immediately. The default basic log is skipped (noBasicLog).

scenarios.name: UEX_WindowsSandbox
scenarios.description: Use when Windows Sandbox fails to start, closes unexpectedly, shows a black or error screen, or has problems with networking, mapped folders or the virtual GPU. Windows Sandbox is a lightweight virtual machine built on the Hyper-V hypervisor and the Host Compute Service, so this scenario traces the Hyper-V stack (there is no Sandbox-specific component). ETW traces: Hyper-V broadly with about 77 providers (SHA_HyperV), including the Host Compute Service, the Virtual Machine Management Service and worker process, the hypervisor and VID, VMBus, virtual disks, storage and VSMB file sharing, the virtual switch and Host Network Service, GPU partitioning, dynamic memory, guest crash dump and the integration services. SHA_HyperV has no data collection function, so apart from the default basic log no Hyper-V event logs or configuration are collected. Tools: Process Monitor (Procmon, ring buffer 3096 MB by default) and Problem Steps Recorder (PSR) screenshots of the repro.

scenarios.name: UEX_WinRM
scenarios.description: Use when WinRM or PowerShell remoting fails, for example Enter-PSSession or Invoke-Command connection, listener or authentication errors (Kerberos, NTLM, CredSSP, certificates and HTTPS), or Windows Event Forwarding subscriptions that do not deliver events.
